translations.literal: Miao Shou, son: Lü. Wang Junwan, son: Zhan. Zhang Shouyue, Wang Wenyu, Zhou Yongqing, Liu Shaoneng, Wang Guangzu, Li Hao, He Bin, son: Shen. Liu Zhongwu, Qu Zhen, Liu Qu, Guo Cheng, Jia Yan, Zhang Zheng, Zhang Yun, Wang En, Yang Yingxun, Zhao Long.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Shou (son: Lü); Wang Junwan (son: Zhan); Zhang Shouyue; Wang Wenyu; Zhou Yongqing; Liu Shaoneng; Wang Guangzu; Li Hao; He Bin (son: Shen); Liu Zhongwu; Qu Zhen; Liu Qu; Guo Cheng; Jia Yan; Zhang Zheng; Zhang Yun; Wang En; Yang Yingxun; and Zhao Long.

sentences.zh: 苗授，字授之，潞州人。

translations.literal: Miao Shou, style name Shouzhi, was a man of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Shou, courtesy name Shouzhi, was a native of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 父京，慶曆中，以死守麟州抗元昊者也。

translations.literal: His father Jing, in the Qingli era, was one who died defending Linzhou resisting Yuanhao.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing had died defending Linzhou against Yuan Hao during the Qingli reign.

sentences.zh: 少從胡翼之學，補國子生，以蔭至供備庫副使。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Hu Yizhi, was enrolled as a Guozi student, and through yin privilege reached Vice Commissioner of the Supply Reserve Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied under Hu Yizhi, entered the Imperial University as a supplemental student, and through hereditary privilege rose to Vice Commissioner of the Supply Reserve Bureau.

sentences.zh: 王韶取鎮洮，授為先鋒，破香子城，拔河府。

translations.literal: When Wang Shao took Zhen and Tao, Shou served as vanguard, broke Xiangzi city, and captured Hefu.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shao seized Zhen and Tao, Shou served as vanguard, capturing Xiangzi city and taking Hefu.

sentences.zh: 羌雖敗，氣尚銳，輒圍香子以迎歸師。

translations.literal: Though the Qiang had been defeated, their spirit was still keen; they promptly besieged Xiangzi to intercept the returning army.
translations.idiomatic: Although the Qiang had been beaten, their fighting spirit remained high, and they promptly laid siege to Xiangzi to cut off the army on its march home.

sentences.zh: 韶遣將田瓊救之，瓊死，乃簡騎五百屬授，授奮擊敗之。

translations.literal: Shao sent the general Tian Qiong to rescue them; Qiong died, whereupon he selected five hundred cavalry and assigned them to Shou, who charged fiercely and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent the general Tian Qiong to relieve them, but Qiong was killed. He then picked five hundred horsemen and placed them under Shou, who charged hard and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 休士二日，羌復要于架麻平，注矢如雨，眾懼，授令曰：「第進毋恐！

translations.literal: After resting the troops two days, the Qiang again challenged them at Jiamaping; arrows poured down like rain, the men were afraid, and Shou ordered: "Advance only—do not fear!
translations.idiomatic: After giving the troops two days' rest, the Qiang again offered battle at Jiamaping. Arrows fell like rain, and the men were terrified. Shou ordered, "Press forward—do not be afraid!

sentences.zh: 氈牌數百且至。」

translations.literal: Several hundred felt shields will arrive shortly."
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred felt shields are on their way."

sentences.zh: 行前者傳呼，羌驚亂。

translations.literal: Those in front passed the word, and the Qiang were startled into confusion.
translations.idiomatic: The men in the van passed the word along, and the Qiang were thrown into panic and disorder.

sentences.zh: 力戰數十，斬首四千級。

translations.literal: After fierce fighting for dozens of rounds, they cut off four thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: After dozens of fierce engagements, they took four thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 又破之于牛精穀，取珂諾城，盡得河湟地。

translations.literal: They again defeated them at Niujing Valley, took Kenuo city, and completely secured the He-Huang region.
translations.idiomatic: They defeated the Qiang again at Niujing Valley, captured Kenuo city, and brought the entire He-Huang region under control.

sentences.zh: 知德順軍，三遷西上閣門使。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Deshun Army and was promoted three times to Western Upper Gate Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military prefect of Deshun and was promoted three times to Western Upper Gate Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 鬼章寇河州，詔授往，一戰克撒宗，論功第一，遂知州事。

translations.literal: Guizhang raided Hezhou; the court ordered Shou to go. In one battle he captured Sazong; ranked first in merit, he then administered the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Guizhang raided Hezhou, the court ordered Shou to march against him. In a single battle he took Sazong, was ranked first in merit, and was put in charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 加四方館使、榮州刺史。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Commissioner of the Four Directions Hall and Prefect of Rongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed Commissioner of the Four Directions Hall and Prefect of Rongzhou.

sentences.zh: 從燕達取銀川，降木征，獻之京師，加引進使、果州團練使、涇原都鈐轄。

translations.literal: Following Yan Da he took Yinchuan, received the surrender of Muzheng, and presented him at the capital; he was made Introducing Commissioner, Militia Commissioner of Guozhou, and Overall Commander of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Yan Da in taking Yinchuan, accepted the surrender of Muzheng, and presented him at court. He was promoted to Introducing Commissioner, Militia Commissioner of Guozhou, and overall commander of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 召使契丹，神宗勞之曰：「曩香子之役，非汝以寡擊眾，幾敗吾事。」

translations.literal: Summoned as envoy to the Khitan, Emperor Shenzong comforted him, saying: "In the former campaign at Xiangzi, had you not used the few to strike the many, my affair would nearly have been ruined."
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned as envoy to the Khitan, Emperor Shenzong praised him, saying, "At Xiangzi, if you had not used a small force to defeat a large one, my whole campaign would nearly have failed."

sentences.zh: 以為秦鳳副總管，徙熙河，復知河州。

translations.literal: He was made Deputy Overall Commander of Qin and Feng, transferred to Xihe, and again administered Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Deputy Overall Commander of Qin and Feng, transferred to Xihe, and again put in charge of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 副李憲討生羌於露骨山，斬首萬級，獲其大酋泠雞樸，羌族十萬七千帳內附，威震洮西。

translations.literal: As deputy to Li Xian he campaigned against the Sheng Qiang at Lugu Mountain, cut off ten thousand heads, captured their great chief Lengjipu, and one hundred seven thousand Qiang households submitted; his prestige shook Taoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Li Xian, he campaigned against the Sheng Qiang at Lugu Mountain, took ten thousand heads, and captured their great chief Lengjipu. One hundred seven thousand Qiang households submitted, and his fame spread throughout western Tao.

sentences.zh: 拜昌州團練使、龍神衛四廂都指揮使，徙知雄州、熙州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Militia Commissioner of Changzhou and Overall Commander of the Four Wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard, and transferred to administer Xiongzhou and Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Militia Commissioner of Changzhou and Overall Commander of the Four Wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard, then transferred to govern Xiongzhou and Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 元豐西討，授出古渭取定西，蕩禹臧花麻諸族，降戶五萬。

translations.literal: In the Yuanfeng western campaign, Shou marched out from Guwei to take Dingxi, swept the Yuzang, Huama, and other tribes, and received the surrender of fifty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfeng western expedition, Shou marched out from Guwei to seize Dingxi, swept the Yuzang, Huama, and other tribes, and accepted the surrender of fifty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 城蘭州，遇賊數萬于女遮谷，登山逆戰，敗退伏壘中，半夜遁去。

translations.literal: While fortifying Lanzhou he encountered tens of thousands of bandits at Nüzhe Valley; he ascended the mountain to meet them in battle, was defeated, withdrew and lay hidden in the fort, and at midnight slipped away.
translations.idiomatic: While building up Lanzhou he met tens of thousands of enemy troops at Nüzhe Valley. He climbed the heights to give battle, was beaten back, hid within the fortifications, and slipped away at midnight.

sentences.zh: 授逾天都山，焚南牟，屯沒煙，凡師行百日，轉鬥千里，始入塞。

translations.literal: Shou crossed Tiandu Mountain, burned Nanmou, and encamped at Meiyan; in all the army marched a hundred days, fought a thousand li, and only then entered the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: Shou crossed Tiandu Mountain, burned Nanmou, and encamped at Meiyan. His army had been in the field a hundred days, fighting its way a thousand li, before it finally re-entered the frontier.

sentences.zh: 授遇事持議不苟合。

translations.literal: In affairs Shou held to his views and would not agree casually.
translations.idiomatic: In council Shou held firm to his views and would not yield merely to agree with others.

sentences.zh: 初在德順，或議城篯南，授曰：「地阻大河，糧道不濟，非萬全計也。」

translations.literal: When he was first at Deshun, some proposed fortifying Zhainan; Shou said: "The ground is blocked by the great river, the supply route cannot be maintained—it is not a plan of complete security."
translations.idiomatic: While he was at Deshun, some proposed building a fort at Zhainan. Shou said, "The terrain is cut off by the great river and the supply line cannot be kept open. That is not a fully reliable plan."

sentences.zh: 役即止。

translations.literal: The work was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 師征靈武，詔令援高遵裕，即條上進退利害甚切。

translations.literal: When the army campaigned against Lingwu, an edict ordered him to reinforce Gao Zunyu; he at once submitted a detailed memorial on the advantages and disadvantages of advance and retreat, very incisively.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched on Lingwu, he was ordered to reinforce Gao Zunyu and immediately submitted a detailed memorial on the risks and benefits of advancing or holding back, in terms that were sharply argued.

sentences.zh: 曆進步軍副都指揮使、威武軍節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: In succession he was promoted to Deputy Overall Commander of the Foot Soldiers and Military Governor and Observation Commissioner of Weiwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to Deputy Overall Commander of the Foot Soldiers and Military Governor and Observation Commissioner of Weiwu Army.

sentences.zh: 元祐三年，遷武泰軍節度使、殿前副都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanyou he was transferred to Military Governor of Wutai Army and Deputy Overall Commander of the Palace Front.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Yuanyou era he was made Military Governor of Wutai Army and Deputy Overall Commander of the Palace Front.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，以保康節度知潞州，提舉上清太平宮，復使殿前，薨，年六十七，贈開府儀同三司，諡曰莊敏。

translations.literal: After a year he was made Military Governor of Baokang and administered Luzhou, was put in charge of the Shangqing Taiping Palace, and again served at the Palace Front; he died at age sixty-seven, was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Palace with Equal Ceremony to the Three Dukes, and given the posthumous title Zhuangmin.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was appointed Military Governor of Baokang and put in charge of Luzhou, was made superintendent of the Shangqing Taiping Palace, and again served at the Palace Front. He died at sixty-seven, was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Palace with Equal Ceremony to the Three Dukes, and was given the posthumous title Zhuangmin.

sentences.zh: 子履。

translations.literal: His son was Lü.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Lü.

sentences.zh: 子 履

translations.literal: Son: Lü
translations.idiomatic: Son: Lü

sentences.zh: 履束發從戎。

translations.literal: Lü, upon binding his hair, followed the army.
translations.idiomatic: Lü took up arms while still a youth.

sentences.zh: 授之降木征也，履護送至京，得閣門祗候。

translations.literal: When Shou received Muzheng's surrender, Lü escorted him to the capital and was made a Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Shou accepted Muzheng's surrender, Lü escorted the captive to the capital and was appointed a Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 曆熙、延、渭、秦四路鈐轄，知鎮戎軍。

translations.literal: In succession he served as Overall Commander on the Xi, Yan, Wei, and Qin circuits and as prefect of Zhenrong Army.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as overall commander on the Xi, Yan, Wei, and Qin circuits and as military prefect of Zhenrong.

sentences.zh: 及其父時，已官四方館使、吉州防禦使矣，以事竄房州，起為西上閣門副使、熙河都監。

translations.literal: By the time of his father's tenure he had already reached Commissioner of the Four Directions Hall and Defense Commissioner of Jizhou; for an offense he was banished to Fangzhou, then recalled as Deputy Western Upper Gate Commissioner and Overall Supervisor of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: Even during his father's lifetime he had risen to Commissioner of the Four Directions Hall and Defense Commissioner of Jizhou. For an offense he was exiled to Fangzhou, then recalled as Deputy Western Upper Gate Commissioner and overall supervisor of Xihe.

sentences.zh: 又責右清道率府率，監峽州酒稅。

translations.literal: He was again demoted to Commandant of the Right Qingdao Commandery and made supervisor of the wine tax at Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted again to Commandant of the Right Qingdao Commandery and put in charge of the wine tax at Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 元符初，悉還其官，以熙河蘭會都鈐轄知蘭州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanfu all his offices were restored; he was made Overall Commander of Xihe, Lan, and Hui and administered Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yuanfu era all his offices were restored, and he was appointed overall commander of Xihe, Lan, and Hui and put in charge of Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔同王贍取青唐，與姚雄合兵討峗羌篯羅結。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to join Wang Zhan in taking Qingtang; with Yao Xiong he combined forces to campaign against the Qiang chief Zhanluojie of Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to join Wang Zhan in taking Qingtang and, together with Yao Xiong, combined forces to campaign against the Zhan Qiang chief Zhanluojie.

sentences.zh: 贍將李忠戰敗，羅結大集眾，宣言欲圍青唐。

translations.literal: Zhan's general Li Zhong was defeated in battle; Luojie gathered a great host and proclaimed his intent to besiege Qingtang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's general Li Zhong was defeated, and Luojie mustered a large force, declaring that he intended to besiege Qingtang.

sentences.zh: 履、雄將至，羌列陣以待，勢甚盛。

translations.literal: As Lü and Xiong were about to arrive, the Qiang drew up battle lines to await them, their momentum very strong.
translations.idiomatic: As Lü and Xiong approached, the Qiang formed battle lines to meet them, and their array looked formidable.

sentences.zh: 履叱軍士納弓于鞬，拔刀而入。

translations.literal: Lü shouted at the soldiers to sheath their bows in their quivers and, drawing their blades, advance in.
translations.idiomatic: Lü ordered his men to stow their bows in their quivers, draw their swords, and charge in.

sentences.zh: 羌怙巢穴殊死鬥，梟將陳迪、王亨輩皆反走，履獨駐馬不動。

translations.literal: The Qiang, relying on their home ground, fought to the death; the fierce generals Chen Di, Wang Heng, and others all turned and fled, while Lü alone sat his horse unmoving.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang, fighting from their home ground, battled desperately. The crack generals Chen Di, Wang Heng, and others all broke and ran, but Lü alone held his horse steady and did not move.

sentences.zh: 有酋青袍白馬突而前，手劍擊履，帳下王拱以弓格之，僅免。

translations.literal: A chief in a green robe on a white horse rushed forward, striking at Lü with a sword in hand; Wang Gong of his staff parried with a bow, and he barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: A chief in a green robe on a white horse charged forward and struck at Lü with a sword. Wang Gong of his staff blocked the blow with a bow, and Lü barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 復繞出履背，欲斷軍為二，別將高永年率所部力戰數十合，羌退，乘勝圍蘭宗堡，弗能拔。

translations.literal: They again circled behind Lü, intending to cut the army in two; the separate commander Gao Yongnian led his unit in fierce fighting for dozens of rounds, the Qiang withdrew, and pressing the advantage they besieged Lanzong Fort but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy circled behind Lü, trying to cut his force in two. The subordinate commander Gao Yongnian led his men through dozens of fierce engagements until the Qiang withdrew. Pursuing the advantage, they besieged Lanzong Fort but could not capture it.

sentences.zh: 日暮，收兵入營，羌宵潰。

translations.literal: At dusk they withdrew the troops into camp; the Qiang fled in the night.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk they withdrew into camp, and the Qiang broke and fled during the night.

sentences.zh: 明日，縱兵四掠，焚其族帳而還。

translations.literal: The next day they unleashed the troops to plunder on all sides, burned their tribal tents, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they sent their troops out in all directions to raid, burned the enemy encampments, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 既而阿章叛，詔履與种樸過河討蕩，辭以兵少，樸遂陷。

translations.literal: Soon after, Azhan rebelled; an edict ordered Lü and Chong Pu to cross the river to suppress and sweep them clean. Lü declined on grounds of too few troops, and Pu was then trapped.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Azhan rebelled. Lü and Chong Pu were ordered to cross the river and suppress the revolt. Lü declined on the grounds that he had too few troops, and Pu was then trapped.

sentences.zh: 錄履前功，擢龍神衛四廂都指揮使、成州團練使，知慶州，徙渭州，進捧日、天武都指揮使。

translations.literal: Recording Lü's former merit, he was promoted to Overall Commander of the Four Wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard and Militia Commissioner of Chengzhou, administered Qingzhou, was transferred to Weizhou, and advanced to Overall Commander of the Sun-bearer and Heavenly Martial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of Lü's earlier service he was promoted to Overall Commander of the Four Wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard and Militia Commissioner of Chengzhou, put in charge of Qingzhou, transferred to Weizhou, and advanced to Overall Commander of the Sun-bearer and Heavenly Martial Guards.

sentences.zh: 是後史失其傳。

translations.literal: After this the histories lose his record.
translations.idiomatic: After this the histories preserve no further account of him.

sentences.zh: 子傅，在《叛臣傳》。

translations.literal: His son Fu is treated in the "Biographies of Rebels."
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu is treated in the "Biographies of Rebels."

sentences.zh: 王君萬

translations.literal: Wang Junwan
translations.idiomatic: Wang Junwan

sentences.zh: 王君萬，秦州寧遠人。

translations.literal: Wang Junwan was a man of Ningyuan in Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Junwan was a native of Ningyuan in Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 以殿侍為秦鳳指揮使。

translations.literal: As a palace attendant he served as commander of the Qin-Feng command.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a palace attendant, he became commander of the Qin-Feng command.

sentences.zh: 王韶開邊，青唐大酋俞龍珂歸國，獨別羌新羅結不從。

translations.literal: When Wang Shao opened the frontier, the great Qingtang chief Yulongke submitted to the state; only the separate Qiang Xinluojie would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shao opened the frontier, the great Qingtang chief Yulongke submitted to the court, but the separate Qiang leader Xinluojie alone refused.

sentences.zh: 經略使韓縝期諸將一月取之。

translations.literal: The frontier commissioner Han Zhen set the generals a deadline of one month to take him.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier commissioner Han Zhen gave the generals one month to capture him.

sentences.zh: 君萬詐為獵者，逐禽至其居，稍相親狎，與同獵，乘間撾之，墜馬，斬首馳歸以獻。

translations.literal: Junwan pretended to be a hunter, pursued game to his dwelling, gradually grew familiar, hunted with him, seized an opening to strike him, knocked him from his horse, cut off his head, and galloped back to present it.
translations.idiomatic: Junwan posed as a hunter, followed game to Xinluojie's camp, gradually won his trust, and hunted with him. Seizing his chance, he struck him down, knocked him from his horse, cut off his head, and galloped back to present it.

sentences.zh: 甫及一月，積功得閣門祗候。

translations.literal: Barely reaching one month, through accumulated merit he was made a Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Barely a month had passed when, on the strength of his merit, he was appointed a Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 王師定武勝，首領藥廝逋邀劫于闐貢物，帥師討焉。

translations.literal: When the imperial army secured Wusheng, the chief Yaosibo intercepted and robbed Khotan tribute goods; Junwan led troops to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: After the imperial army secured Wusheng, the chief Yaosibo had intercepted Khotan's tribute goods. Junwan led troops against him.

sentences.zh: 君萬出南山，履險略地。

translations.literal: Junwan marched out through the southern mountains, treading perilous and trackless ground.
translations.idiomatic: Junwan marched out through the southern mountains, crossing dangerous and trackless terrain.

sentences.zh: 羌潛伏山谷間，忽一騎躍出，橫矛將及，君萬亟側身避之，回首奮擊，斬以徇。

translations.literal: The Qiang lay hidden in the mountain valleys; suddenly a single rider leaped out, his spear athwart and about to reach him; Junwan swiftly turned aside to avoid it, then wheeled back and struck fiercely, cutting him down and displaying the head.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang lay in ambush among the valleys. Suddenly a lone rider leaped out, spear leveled at him. Junwan twisted aside just in time, wheeled back, and struck him down, displaying the head as a warning.

sentences.zh: 其眾驚號，相率聽命，所斬乃藥廝逋也。

translations.literal: His followers cried out in alarm and submitted one after another; the one cut down had been Yaosibo himself.
translations.idiomatic: His followers cried out in alarm and submitted in succession. The man he had killed was Yaosibo himself.

sentences.zh: 復破北關、南市，功最多，擢熙河路鈐轄，進領英州刺史、達州團練使，賜絹五百。

translations.literal: He again broke Beiguan and Nanshi; having the greatest merit, he was promoted to Overall Commander of the Xihe circuit, advanced to Prefect of Yingzhou and Militia Commissioner of Dazhou, and granted five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He also captured Beiguan and Nanshi. Having earned the greatest merit, he was promoted to overall commander of the Xihe circuit, advanced to Prefect of Yingzhou and Militia Commissioner of Dazhou, and granted five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 洮西羌叛，圍河州，君萬請于王韶，以為南撒宗城小而堅，強勇所聚，若並兵破之，圍當自解。

translations.literal: The Taoxi Qiang rebelled and besieged Hezhou; Junwan petitioned Wang Shao, holding that Nansazong city was small but strong, a gathering place of the fierce and brave—if they combined forces to break it, the siege should resolve itself.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taoxi Qiang rebelled and besieged Hezhou, Junwan advised Wang Shao that Nansazong was small but strongly fortified and held the enemy's best fighters. If they concentrated their forces and took it, the siege of Hezhou would lift of itself.

sentences.zh: 韶用其計，圍果解。

translations.literal: Shao used his plan, and the siege indeed lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Shao adopted his plan, and the siege was indeed lifted.

sentences.zh: 累官客省使，為副總管。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he reached Commissioner of the Guest Bureau and served as deputy overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to Commissioner of the Guest Bureau and served as deputy overall commander.

sentences.zh: 坐貸結糴錢數萬緡，為轉運使孫迥所糾，貶秩一等。

translations.literal: He was implicated for lending out tens of thousands of strings of grain-purchase money; impeached by the transport commissioner Sun Jiong, he was demoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was found guilty of lending out tens of thousands of strings of government grain-purchase funds. Impeached by transport commissioner Sun Jiong, he was demoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 討西山、鐵城有功，復故官職。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Xishan and Tiecheng he had merit, and his former offices were restored.
translations.idiomatic: He earned merit in campaigns against Xishan and Tiecheng, and his former offices were restored.

sentences.zh: 君萬怨孫迥，使番官木丹訟之，鞫于秦、隴，又貶為鳳翔鈐轄，籍家貲償逋，遂以憤卒。

translations.literal: Junwan bore a grudge against Sun Jiong and had the frontier officer Mudan bring suit against him; tried in Qin and Long, he was again demoted to Overall Commander of Fengxiang, his family property registered to repay the debt, and he died of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Junwan resented Sun Jiong and had the frontier officer Mudan bring suit against him. Tried in Qin and Long, he was demoted again to overall commander of Fengxiang, his family property seized to repay the debt, and he died in bitterness.

sentences.zh: 子贍。

translations.literal: His son was Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhan.

sentences.zh: 子 贍

translations.literal: Son: Zhan
translations.idiomatic: Son: Zhan

sentences.zh: 贍始因李憲以進。

translations.literal: Zhan at first advanced through Li Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan first rose through the patronage of Li Xian.

sentences.zh: 立戰功，積官至皇城使，領開州團練使。

translations.literal: Establishing battle merit, he accumulated offices to Imperial City Commissioner and held the post of Militia Commissioner of Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He won distinction in battle and rose through repeated promotions to Imperial City Commissioner and Militia Commissioner of Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 元符中，知河州。

translations.literal: In the Yuanfu era he administered Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfu era he was put in charge of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 熙帥鐘傅以冒白草原賞，獄治于秦，詔轉運使張詢諭諸將得自首。

translations.literal: The Xi commander Zhong Fu had falsely claimed reward for the Baiyuan grasslands; the case was tried in Qin, and an edict ordered the transport commissioner Zhang Xun to inform the generals that confession would be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi commander Zhong Fu had falsely claimed credit for the Baiyuan grasslands. The case was tried in Qin, and an edict ordered transport commissioner Zhang Xun to inform the generals that they might confess and be spared.

sentences.zh: 贍具伏詐增首級，因說詢云：「青唐人有叛瞎征意，可取也。」

translations.literal: Zhan fully confessed to fraudulently inflating head counts and thereupon told Xun: "The Qingtang people have the intent to rebel against Xiazheng—it can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Zhan fully confessed to having fraudulently inflated his head count and then told Xun, "The Qingtang people are ready to turn against Xiazheng. Qingtang can be taken."

sentences.zh: 詢信之，即具奏言已令贍結約起兵。

translations.literal: Xun believed him and at once submitted a detailed memorial stating that he had already ordered Zhan to arrange a pact and raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xun believed him and immediately memorialized the throne that he had already ordered Zhan to arrange a pact and raise troops.

sentences.zh: 誓宗與輔臣罪其狂妄專輒，亟罷詢，而命孫迥究實。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhezong and the chief ministers blamed his arrogance and arbitrary action; they quickly dismissed Xun and ordered Sun Jiong to investigate the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhezong and the chief ministers condemned this as reckless and overreaching. Xun was quickly dismissed, and Sun Jiong was ordered to investigate the truth.

sentences.zh: 獄上，奪贍十一官，猶令領州。

translations.literal: When the case was submitted, Zhan was stripped of eleven ranks but still ordered to administer the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was concluded, Zhan was stripped of eleven ranks but was still allowed to govern the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 贍欲以功贖過，乃密畫取青唐之策，遣客詣章惇言狀。

translations.literal: Zhan wished to redeem his fault through merit; he secretly drew up a plan to take Qingtang and sent a client to Zhang Dun to state the case.
translations.idiomatic: Hoping to redeem himself through merit, Zhan secretly drew up a plan to take Qingtang and sent an agent to Zhang Dun to lay out the proposal.

sentences.zh: 惇下其事于孫路，路以為可取。

translations.literal: Dun referred the matter to Sun Lu, and Lu judged it feasible.
translations.idiomatic: Dun referred the matter to Sun Lu, who judged the plan feasible.

sentences.zh: 贍遂引兵趣邈川。

translations.literal: Zhan then led troops toward Miaochuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan then led his troops toward Miaochuan.

sentences.zh: 路知贍狡獪難制，使總管王湣統軍，而以贍副。

translations.literal: Lu knew Zhan was crafty and hard to control; he had the overall commander Wang Min command the army and made Zhan his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Zhan was cunning and hard to control, Lu put overall commander Wang Min in command of the army and made Zhan his deputy.

sentences.zh: 贍為前鋒度河，先下隴朱黑城。

translations.literal: Zhan as vanguard crossed the river and first took Longzhuhei city.
translations.idiomatic: As vanguard, Zhan crossed the river and was first to take Longzhuhei city.

sentences.zh: 忌湣分其功，紿之曰：「晨食畢乃發。」

translations.literal: Jealous that Min would share his merit, he deceived him, saying: "We will set out only after morning meal is finished."
translations.idiomatic: Jealous that Min would share the credit, he deceived him, saying, "We will not march until after breakfast."

sentences.zh: 湣信之。

translations.literal: Min believed him.
translations.idiomatic: Min believed him.

sentences.zh: 夜半，贍忽傳發。

translations.literal: At midnight Zhan suddenly ordered the march.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight Zhan suddenly ordered the army to move out.

sentences.zh: 平明，入邈川，據府庫，徑上捷書，不以白軍府。

translations.literal: At daybreak he entered Miaochuan, seized the government stores, and sent a victory report directly, without informing the army headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak he entered Miaochuan, seized the government stores, and sent a victory report directly to court without informing army headquarters.

sentences.zh: 湣過午始至，以事訴于路，路亦怒，顓以兵柄付湣，而留贍屯邈川。

translations.literal: Min did not arrive until past noon; he complained of the affair to Lu, and Lu was also angry; he solely entrusted military authority to Min and left Zhan to garrison Miaochuan.
translations.idiomatic: Min did not arrive until past noon and complained to Lu, who was also furious. Lu gave sole command of the army to Min and left Zhan to garrison Miaochuan.

sentences.zh: 宗哥酋舍欽腳求內附，贍遣裨將王詠享五千騎赴之。

translations.literal: The Zongge chief Sheqinjiao sought to submit inward; Zhan sent the subordinate general Wang Yongxiang with five thousand cavalry to go to him.
translations.idiomatic: The Zongge chief Sheqinjiao sought to submit to the court. Zhan sent subordinate general Wang Yongxiang with five thousand cavalry to receive him.

sentences.zh: 既入，而諸羌變，詠馳書告急，王厚使高永年救之，乃免。

translations.literal: Once they had entered, the various Qiang turned on them; Yongxiang sent a galloping letter in emergency; Wang Hou sent Gao Yongnian to rescue them, and they barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside, the Qiang turned on them. Yongxiang sent an urgent dispatch for help, and Wang Hou sent Gao Yongnian to rescue him. They barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 贍與湣交訟，又訴路指畫相違。

translations.literal: Zhan and Min exchanged lawsuits, and Zhan again complained to Lu that their plans conflicted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan and Min sued each other back and forth, and Zhan again complained to Lu that their plans had been at cross purposes.

sentences.zh: 惇主贍而不直路，曰：「首謀者贍也，路欲掩其功，故抑贍。」

translations.literal: Dun took Zhan's side and did not vindicate Lu, saying: "The chief plotter was Zhan; Lu wished to cover his merit, and therefore suppressed Zhan."
translations.idiomatic: Dun sided with Zhan and refused to vindicate Lu, saying, "Zhan was the chief architect of the plan. Lu wanted to steal his credit, and so he held Zhan back."

sentences.zh: 乃徙路河南，罷湣統制，以胡宗回為帥。

translations.literal: Lu was then transferred to Henan, Min's overall command was abolished, and Hu Zonghui was made commander.
translations.idiomatic: Lu was transferred to Henan, Min was removed from overall command, and Hu Zonghui was appointed commander.

sentences.zh: 時瞎征已來降，青唐戍將惟心牟欽氈父子百余人在。

translations.literal: At the time Xiazheng had already come to surrender; more than a hundred men including the Qingtang garrison commander Weixinmuqinzan and his son were within.
translations.idiomatic: By then Xiazheng had already surrendered, and more than a hundred men, including the Qingtang garrison commander Weixinmuqinzan and his son, were still inside the city.

sentences.zh: 贍不即取，二羌遂迎溪巴溫之子隴拶入守。

translations.literal: Zhan did not take it at once; the two Qiang then welcomed Xibawen's son Longzan to enter and hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan did not move quickly to take the city, and the two Qiang factions then welcomed Xibawen's son Longzan to enter and hold it.

sentences.zh: 始，孫路乞先全邈川及河南北諸城，然後進師。

translations.literal: At the outset Sun Lu had requested first to secure Miaochuan and all the cities north and south of Henan, and only then advance the army.
translations.idiomatic: From the start Sun Lu had asked first to secure Miaochuan and all the cities north and south of the river, and only then advance.

sentences.zh: 贍怨路，因言青唐不煩大兵可下，而路逗遛失機會。

translations.literal: Zhan resented Lu and therefore said Qingtang could be taken without troubling a great army, while Lu had dallied and lost the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan resented Lu and claimed that Qingtang could be taken without a large army, while Lu had dragged his feet and missed the chance.

sentences.zh: 暨宗回至，乃雲夏人謀攻邈川，當為守備，青唐未可取。

translations.literal: When Zonghui arrived, he then said the Xia people were plotting to attack Miaochuan and that they should make defensive preparations—Qingtang could not yet be taken.
translations.idiomatic: But when Zonghui arrived, he claimed that the Xia were plotting to attack Miaochuan, that defensive preparations were needed, and that Qingtang could not yet be taken.

sentences.zh: 宗回責其反覆，日夜督出師，遣使威以軍法，且聲言欲使王湣代將。

translations.literal: Zonghui reproached his inconsistency, day and night pressed him to march out, sent envoys to threaten him with military law, and moreover proclaimed his intent to have Wang Min replace him as commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghui rebuked him for his inconsistency and pressed him day and night to take the field. He sent envoys to threaten him with military law and openly declared that he intended to replace him with Wang Min.

sentences.zh: 贍懼，急進攻隴拶及心牟等，皆出降。

translations.literal: Zhan was afraid; he urgently advanced to attack Longzan and Xinmu and the others; all came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful, Zhan pressed forward at once to attack Longzan, Xinmu, and their followers; all of them came out and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 贍入據其城。

translations.literal: Zhan entered and occupied the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan entered and took possession of the city.

sentences.zh: 詔建為鄯州，進贍四方館使、榮州防禦使、知州事。

translations.literal: An edict established it as Shan Prefecture; Zhan was promoted to Commissioner of the Four Embassies, Defense Commissioner of Rongzhou, and Administrator of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the city established as Shan Prefecture and promoted Zhan to Commissioner of the Four Embassies, Defense Commissioner of Rongzhou, and prefectural administrator.

sentences.zh: 黃履謂賞薄，乃拜維州團練使，為路鈐轄。

translations.literal: Huang Lü said the reward was meager; [the court] then appointed [him] Regimental Commissioner of Weizhou and made him Circuit Controller.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Lü judged the reward too slight, so the court additionally appointed him Regimental Commissioner of Weizhou and made him controller of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 贍縱所部剽敚，羌眾攜貳，心牟等結諸族帳謀復青唐，其在山南者先發。

translations.literal: Zhan let his troops plunder and seize; the Qiang masses became divided and disloyal; Xinmu and others united the clans and tents to plot retaking Qingtang; those south of the mountains acted first.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan allowed his troops to loot at will. The Qiang turned divided and disaffected, and Xinmu and others rallied the clans and encampments to plot the recovery of Qingtang; those south of the mountains rose first.

sentences.zh: 贍遣將李賓領二千騎掩襲心牟以下，自守西城與羌鬥。

translations.literal: Zhan sent the general Li Bin leading two thousand cavalry to launch a surprise attack on Xinmu and those below him, while he himself held the western city and fought the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan dispatched the general Li Bin with two thousand horsemen to strike Xinmu and his followers by surprise, while he himself held the western city and fought the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 賓逾南山入保敦穀討蕩，羌戰敗奔北，四山皆空。

translations.literal: Bin crossed South Mountain and entered Baodungu to hunt them down; the Qiang were defeated and fled north; the four mountains were all emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Bin crossed South Mountain and entered Baodungu to mop them up. The Qiang were beaten and fled north, and the mountains on all four sides were emptied.

sentences.zh: 贍戮心牟等九人，悉捕斬城中羌，積級如山。

translations.literal: Zhan executed Xinmu and eight others; he apprehended and beheaded all the Qiang in the city; severed heads piled up like a mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan put Xinmu and eight others to death, then seized and beheaded every Qiang still in the city until severed heads were heaped like a hill.

sentences.zh: 初，贍諷諸酋籍勝兵者涅其臂，無應者。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhan had hinted to the various chiefs that those registered as able-bodied soldiers should tattoo their arms; none responded.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhan had hinted to the chiefs that men registered as fit for battle should tattoo their arms, but no one complied.

sentences.zh: 篯羅結請歸帥本路為唱，贍聽之去，遂嘯集外叛，以數千人圍邈川，夏眾十萬助之，城中危甚。

translations.literal: Zhanluojie requested to return and lead his native circuit as rallying cry; Zhan let him go; he then gathered outside rebels, and with several thousand men besieged Miaochuan; a hundred thousand Xia troops aided them; the city was in grave peril.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanluojie asked leave to return home and lead his native circuit as a rallying cry; Zhan allowed him to go. He then mustered rebels from outside, and with several thousand men besieged Miaochuan while a hundred thousand Xia troops came to their aid. The city was in extreme danger.

sentences.zh: 苗履、姚雄來援，圍始解。

translations.literal: Miao Lü and Yao Xiong came to relieve them; the siege was only then lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Lü and Yao Xiong arrived with reinforcements, and only then was the siege broken.

sentences.zh: 已而王吉、魏釗、种樸相繼敗沒，將士奪氣。

translations.literal: Before long Wang Ji, Wei Zhao, and Zhong Pu were defeated and lost in succession; officers and soldiers lost their fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wang Ji, Wei Zhao, and Zhong Pu were defeated and killed in turn, and officers and soldiers lost heart.

sentences.zh: 書聞，帝震駭，於是轉運使李譓、秦希甫劾贍盜取二城財物，因此致變；

translations.literal: When the report arrived, the emperor was greatly shocked; thereupon the transport commissioner Li Kui and Qin Xifu impeached Zhan for plundering the goods of the two cities, thereby causing the uprising;
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, the emperor was deeply alarmed. The transport commissioner Li Kui and Qin Xifu then impeached Zhan for looting the wealth of the two cities and thereby provoking the revolt;

sentences.zh: 又殺心牟欽氈以滅口。

translations.literal: They further charged that he had killed Xinmu Qinzan to silence him.
translations.idiomatic: they also charged that he had killed Xinmu Qinzan to silence him.

sentences.zh: 曾布言贍創造事端以生邊害，萬死不塞責。

translations.literal: Zeng Bu said Zhan had created trouble to bring harm to the frontier; ten thousand deaths would not suffice to answer for it.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Bu declared that Zhan had deliberately stirred up trouble and brought calamity to the frontier, and that even death ten thousand times over would not atone for it.

sentences.zh: 詔貶右千牛將軍，房州安置。

translations.literal: An edict demoted him to Right General of the Thousand-Ox Guard and assigned him to residence in Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict demoted him to Right General of the Thousand-Ox Guard and ordered him confined to Fang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 言者論之不已，熙河又奏青唐諸族怨贍入骨髓，日圖報復，樞密院乞斬贍以謝一方。

translations.literal: Critics kept arguing without cease; Xihe also reported that the Qingtang tribes hated Zhan to the marrow and plotted revenge daily; the Bureau of Military Affairs requested that Zhan be beheaded to appease the region.
translations.idiomatic: Critics would not let the matter rest. Xihe also reported that the Qingtang tribes hated Zhan to the bone and plotted revenge every day, and the Bureau of Military Affairs asked that he be executed to appease the region.

sentences.zh: 詔配昌化軍，行至穰縣而縊。

translations.literal: An edict exiled him to Changhua Army; en route, at Xiang County, he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: An edict banished him to Changhua Army, but on the road at Xiang County he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 崇甯初，蔡京入相，錢遹訟贍功；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongning, when Cai Jing entered the chancellorship, Qian Tong petitioned regarding Zhan's merits;
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Chongning era, after Cai Jing became chief councilor, Qian Tong petitioned on behalf of Zhan's achievements;

sentences.zh: 及王厚平鄯、廓，於是追贈保平軍節度觀察留後，除其子玨通事舍人。

translations.literal: When Wang Hou pacified Shan and Kuo, [the court] thereupon posthumously enfeoffed [Zhan] as Military Commissioner and Observation Regent of Baoping Army, and appointed his son Jue as Attendant at the Office of Transmission Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: and when Wang Hou pacified Shan and Kuo, the court posthumously enfeoffed Zhan as Military Commissioner and Observation Regent of Baoping Army and appointed his son Jue as Attendant at the Office of Transmission Affairs.

sentences.zh: 張守約

translations.literal: Zhang Shouyue
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shouyue

sentences.zh: 張守約，字希參，濮州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shouyue, style name Xican, was a man of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shouyue, courtesy name Xican, was a native of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 以蔭主原州截原砦，招羌酋水令逋等十七族萬一千帳。

translations.literal: Through yin privilege he served as garrison commander of Jiayuan Fort in Yuanzhou; he recruited seventeen tribes including the Qiang chieftain Shuilingbo, totaling eleven thousand tents.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he became commander of Jiayuan Fort in Yuan Prefecture and recruited seventeen tribes, including the Qiang chieftain Shuilingbo, totaling eleven thousand tents.

sentences.zh: 為廣南走馬承受公事，當儂寇之後，二年四詣闕，陳南方利害，皆見納用，歐陽修薦其有智略、知邊事，擢知融州。

translations.literal: He served as Guangnan mobile inspection commissioner; after the Nong raids, within two years he visited court four times, expounding the advantages and disadvantages of the south; all were accepted and acted upon; Ouyang Xiu recommended him for his resourcefulness and knowledge of frontier affairs; he was promoted to administer Rongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Guangnan mobile inspection commissioner. In the aftermath of the Nong rebellion he visited court four times within two years to set out the strategic interests of the south, and each proposal was accepted. Ouyang Xiu recommended him for his shrewdness and knowledge of frontier affairs, and he was promoted to administer Rong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 峒將吳儂恃險為邊患，捕誅之。

translations.literal: The cave general Wu Nong relied on difficult terrain to be a frontier menace; [Shouyue] captured and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: The cave chieftain Wu Nong relied on rugged terrain to plague the frontier; Shouyue captured and executed him.

sentences.zh: 修復薦守約可任將帥，為定州路駐泊都監，徙秦鳳。

translations.literal: Xiu again recommended Shouyue as fit for command; he was made Chief Garrison Commander of Dingzhou Circuit, then transferred to Qin-Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu again recommended Shouyue as fit for high command. He was made chief garrison commander on the Dingzhou circuit and then transferred to Qin-Feng.

sentences.zh: 居職六年，括生羌隱土千頃以募射手，築硤石堡、甘穀城，第功最多。

translations.literal: In six years in office he surveyed a thousand qing of hidden land among the raw Qiang to recruit archers, built Xiashi Fort and Gangu city; his merit was ranked highest.
translations.idiomatic: In six years of service he registered a thousand qing of concealed land among the raw Qiang to recruit archers, built Xiashi Fort and Gangu city, and ranked first in merit.

sentences.zh: 夏人萬騎來寇，守約適巡邊，與之遇，不解鞍，簡兵五百逆戰，眾寡不侔，勢小卻。

translations.literal: Ten thousand Xia horsemen came raiding; Shouyue happened to be inspecting the border and encountered them; without dismounting, he selected five hundred soldiers to meet them in battle; their numbers were unequal and his force fell back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand Xia horsemen came raiding. Shouyue happened to be on a border inspection and met them. Without even dismounting, he picked five hundred men to meet the attack, but being badly outnumbered his force gave a little ground.

sentences.zh: 夏人張兩翼來，守約挺身立陣前，自節金鼓，發強弩殪其酋，敵遂退。

translations.literal: The Xia deployed both wings; Shouyue stood forth in front of the formation, himself regulating drums and gongs, loosed powerful crossbows and killed their chieftain; the enemy then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia opened both wings. Shouyue stepped to the front of the line, himself beat the drums and gongs, and with powerful crossbows brought down their chieftain. The enemy then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 神宗開拓熙河，召問曰：「王韶能辦事否？」

translations.literal: The Emperor Shenzong, opening the Hexi campaign, summoned him and asked: "Can Wang Shao get things done?"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong opened the campaign to develop the Xihe region, he summoned Shouyue and asked, "Can Wang Shao carry the task through?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「以天威臨之，當無不濟；

translations.literal: He replied: "With imperial might bearing down on them, nothing should fail to succeed;
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "With the majesty of the throne bearing down on them, nothing should fail;

sentences.zh: 但董氈忠勤效順，恐不宜侵逼。」

translations.literal: but Dongzhan is loyal, diligent, and submissive—I fear it is not fitting to press and encroach upon him."
translations.idiomatic: but Dongzhan has been loyal, diligent, and obedient, and I fear it would be unwise to press and encroach upon him."

sentences.zh: 因請名古渭為軍，以根本隴右。

translations.literal: He therefore requested that ancient Wei be named a military prefecture to secure Longyou as the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked that ancient Wei be made a military prefecture so that Longyou might be secured at its root.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，建為通遠軍。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this; it was established as Tongyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and it was established as Tongyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 加通事舍人、熙河鈐轄，仍統秦鳳羌兵駐通遠。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Attendant at the Office of Transmission Affairs and Xihe Circuit Controller, still commanding Qin-Feng Qiang troops stationed at Tongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed Attendant at the Office of Transmission Affairs and controller of the Xihe circuit, and continued to command the Qin-Feng Qiang troops stationed at Tongyuan.

sentences.zh: 河州羌率眾三萬屯於敦波，欲復舊地，守約度洮水擊破之，取窖粟食軍。

translations.literal: Qiang of Hezhou led thirty thousand massed at Dunbo, intending to recover their old lands; Shouyue crossed the Tao River and defeated them, taking stored grain to feed the army.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang of He Prefecture mustered thirty thousand men and encamped at Dunbo, intending to recover their old lands. Shouyue crossed the Tao River, routed them, and took grain from their hidden stores to feed his army.

sentences.zh: 羌老弱畜產走南山，左右欲邀之，雲可獲萬萬。

translations.literal: The old, weak, livestock, and goods fled to South Mountain; those at his sides wanted to intercept them, saying tens upon tens of thousands could be captured.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang elderly, women, children, and livestock fled toward South Mountain. His officers wanted to cut them off, saying the booty would run into the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 守約曰：「彼非敢迎戰，逃死耳，輒出者斬！」

translations.literal: Shouyue said: "They did not dare to meet us in battle—they are fleeing for their lives; whoever sallies out will be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Shouyue said, "They did not dare stand and fight—they are running for their lives. Anyone who sallies out without orders will be beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 鬼章圍岷州，守約提敢死士鳴鼓張幟高山上，賊驚顧而遁，遂知岷州，降其首領千七百人。

translations.literal: Guizhang besieged Minzhou; Shouyue led dare-to-die soldiers, beat drums and raised banners on the high mountains; the bandits looked back in alarm and fled; he then administered Minzhou and accepted the surrender of 1,700 chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: When Guizhang besieged Min Prefecture, Shouyue led dare-to-die troops to beat drums and raise banners on the heights. The enemy looked back in alarm and fled. He then became prefect of Min and received the surrender of seventeen hundred chieftains.

sentences.zh: 遷西上閣門使、知鎮戎軍，徙環州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Western Upper Gate Commissioner and Administrator of Zhenrong Army, then moved to Huanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Western Upper Gate Commissioner and put in charge of Zhenrong Army, then transferred to Huan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 慕家族頡佷難制，搖動種落，勒兵討擒之，余遁入夏國。

translations.literal: The Mu family clan was fierce and hard to control, stirring up the tribes; he led troops to campaign, captured them; the remainder fled into Xia territory.
translations.idiomatic: The Mu family was fierce and unruly and stirred up the tribes. He led troops against them, captured them, and the rest fled into Xia territory.

sentences.zh: 守約駐師境上，檄取不置，居數日，械以來，斬於市。

translations.literal: Shouyue stationed his army on the border and sent summons after summons without relenting; after several days they were brought in shackles and beheaded in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyue kept his army on the border and issued demand after demand for their surrender. After several days they were brought in chains and executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 從征靈武，至清遠軍，言于高遵裕曰：「此去靈州不三百里，用以前軍先出，直搗其城。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Lingwu, reaching Qingyuan Army, he said to Gao Zunyu: "From here to Lingzhou is less than three hundred li. Use the vanguard to sally first and strike straight at the city.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Lingwu he reached Qingyuan Army and said to Gao Zunyu, "Ling Prefecture is less than three hundred li from here. Send the vanguard out first and strike straight at the city.

sentences.zh: 今夏人以一方之力，應五路之師，橫山無人，靈州城中惟僧道數百。

translations.literal: Now the Xia with the strength of one region are answering five-route armies; Hengshan has no men; in Lingzhou city there are only several hundred monks and Daoists.
translations.idiomatic: Right now the Xia are stretching the strength of one region to answer five invading armies. Hengshan is empty, and inside Ling Prefecture there are only a few hundred monks and Daoist priests.

sentences.zh: 若裹十日糧，疾馳三日可至，軍無事矣。」

translations.literal: If we pack ten days' rations and ride hard, in three days we can arrive; the army's task would be done."
translations.idiomatic: If we carry ten days' rations and ride hard, we can reach it in three days and the campaign will be over."

sentences.zh: 又勸高遵裕令士眾護糧餉，以防抄掠，不聽，果以敗還。

translations.literal: He also urged Gao Zunyu to have the soldiers protect the grain supplies against raiding; [Gao] would not listen, and indeed they returned in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged Gao Zunyu to have the troops guard the grain convoys against raiders, but Gao would not listen, and in the end the army returned in defeat.

sentences.zh: 守約有捍海南咸平之功，亦不錄。

translations.literal: Shouyue had merit in defending Hainan and Xiaping, yet that too went unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyue had also earned merit defending the Hainan and Xiaping regions, yet even that went unrewarded.

sentences.zh: 進為環慶都鈐轄、知邠州，徙涇原、鄜延、秦鳳副總管，領康州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Huan-Qing Circuit Controller and Administrator of Binzhou, transferred to deputy overall commander of Jingyuan, Yan-Yan, and Qin-Feng, and held office as Administrator of Kangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to controller of the Huan-Qing circuit and prefect of Bin, then made deputy overall commander of Jingyuan, Yan-Yan, and Qin-Feng while also holding office as prefect of Kang.

sentences.zh: 夏人十萬屯南牟，畏其名，引去。

translations.literal: A hundred thousand Xia massed at Nanmou; fearing his name, they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When a hundred thousand Xia encamped at Nanmou, they withdrew at the mere mention of his name.

sentences.zh: 知涇州，涇水善暴城，每春必增治堤堰，費不貲。

translations.literal: As Administrator of Jingzhou, the Jing River frequently breached the walls; each spring dikes and weirs had to be reinforced, costing immeasurable expense.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Jing, he found that the Jing River often burst its banks and threatened the city walls. Every spring the dikes and sluices had to be rebuilt at enormous cost.

sentences.zh: 適歲饑，罷其役。

translations.literal: It happened to be a famine year; he suspended the labor.
translations.idiomatic: A famine year came, and he suspended the work.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「如水害何？」

translations.literal: Some said: "What about flood damage?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked, "But what if the river floods?"

sentences.zh: 守約曰：「歉歲勞民，甚於河患，吾且徐圖之。」

translations.literal: Shouyue said: "In a lean year, exhausting the people is worse than river calamity; I shall plan for it gradually."
translations.idiomatic: Shouyue replied, "In a bad harvest year, exhausting the people is worse than any flood. I will deal with the river in due time."

sentences.zh: 河神祠故在南壖，禱而遷諸北，以殺河怒。

translations.literal: The River God shrine had formerly stood on the south bank; after praying he moved it to the north, to appease the river's wrath.
translations.idiomatic: The shrine of the River God had stood on the south bank. After offering prayers he moved it to the north, hoping to soften the river's fury.

sentences.zh: 一夕雷雨，明日，河徙而南，其北遂為沙磧。

translations.literal: One night of thunder and rain; the next day the river shifted southward, and the north became sandy wastes.
translations.idiomatic: One night brought thunder and rain. The next day the river shifted south, and the ground to the north became sandy waste.

sentences.zh: 以龍、神衛四廂都指揮使召還，道卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: He was summoned back as Commander of the four wings of the Dragon and Divine Guard; he died on the road, age seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as commander of the four wings of the Dragon and Divine Guard, but died on the journey at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 守約典七州，皆有惠愛可紀。

translations.literal: Shouyue administered seven prefectures; in each there was kindness and love worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyue governed seven prefectures, and in each his kindness and care were worth recording.

sentences.zh: 神宗嘗謂武臣可任者，以燕達、劉昌祚、姚麟、王崇極、劉舜卿等對，其後皆為名將，時稱知人。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong once asked which military officials were fit for employment; he answered with Yan Da, Liu Changzuo, Yao Lin, Wang Chongji, Liu Shunqing, and others; all later became famous generals; at the time he was said to know men.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong once asked which military men were fit for appointment, he named Yan Da, Liu Changzuo, Yao Lin, Wang Chongji, Liu Shunqing, and others—all of whom later became celebrated generals—and at the time he was praised for knowing men.

sentences.zh: 王文郁

translations.literal: Wang Wenyu
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wenyu

sentences.zh: 王文郁，字周卿，麟州新秦人。

translations.literal: Wang Wenyu, style name Zhouqing, was a man of Xinqin in Lin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wenyu, courtesy name Zhouqing, was a native of Xinqin in Lin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以供奉官為府州巡檢。

translations.literal: As an attendance officer he served as frontier inspector of Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as an attendance officer, he served as frontier inspector of Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 韓琦薦其材，加閣門祗候、麟府駐泊都監。

translations.literal: Han Qi recommended his talent; he was added as Gate Attendant and Chief Garrison Commander of Lin-Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi recommended his ability, and he was promoted to Gate Attendant and chief garrison commander on the Lin-Fu frontier.

sentences.zh: 熙甯討夏國，文鬱敗之吐渾河。

translations.literal: During the Xining campaign against the Xia state, Wenyu defeated them at the Tu-hun River.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining campaign against Xia, Wenyu defeated the enemy on the Tu-hun River.

sentences.zh: 其將香崖夜遣使以劍為信，欲舉眾降，許之。

translations.literal: His general Xiangya sent an envoy by night with a sword as token, wishing to lead the masses to surrender; [Wenyu] agreed.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinate Xiangya sent an envoy by night with a sword as pledge, offering to bring his forces over in surrender, and Wenyu agreed.

sentences.zh: 旦而至，與偕行，眾情忽變，噪以出。

translations.literal: At dawn he arrived and traveled together [with Wenyu]; the crowd's sentiment suddenly changed and they clamored to sally forth.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Xiangya arrived and set out with him, but the mood of the men suddenly shifted and they clamored to break out.

sentences.zh: 文鬱擊之，追奔二十里。

translations.literal: Wenyu struck them and pursued the fleeing foe twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu attacked them and pursued the fleeing enemy twenty li.

sentences.zh: 據險大戰，矢下如雨，文郁徐引度河，謂吏士曰：「前追強敵，後背天險，韓信驅市人且破趙，況爾曹皆百戰驍勇邪？」

translations.literal: They fought a great battle at difficult terrain; arrows fell like rain; Wenyu slowly led [his men] across the river and said to officers and soldiers: "Ahead we pursue a strong foe; behind us lies heaven's barrier. Han Xin drove market folk and still broke Zhao—how much more so you, all battle-hardened and fierce?"
translations.idiomatic: They fought a fierce battle in rugged terrain while arrows fell like rain. Wenyu slowly led his men across the river and told his officers and soldiers, "Ahead lies a powerful foe; behind us is a natural barrier. Han Xin drove shopkeepers and still broke Zhao—how much more should you, who are all seasoned and fierce in battle?"

sentences.zh: 士感奮進擊，夏人大潰，降其眾二千。

translations.literal: The soldiers, stirred, pressed the attack; the Xia were utterly routed; two thousand of their masses surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The men were roused and pressed the attack. The Xia were utterly routed, and two thousand of them surrendered.

sentences.zh: 遷通事舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant at the Office of Transmission Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant at the Office of Transmission Affairs.

sentences.zh: 夏人逾屈野河，掠塞上，文郁追至長城阪，盡奪所掠而還。

translations.literal: The Xia crossed the Quye River and raided the frontier; Wenyu pursued to Changcheng Slope, fully recovered what had been plundered, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xia crossed the Quye River and raided the frontier, Wenyu pursued them to Changcheng Slope, recovered everything they had taken, and returned.

sentences.zh: 神宗召見，問曰：「向者招納香崖，群議不一，其為朕言之。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong summoned him and asked: "Earlier when recruiting Xiangya, opinion in the assembly was divided—explain this for me."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong summoned him and asked, "When we earlier sought to win over Xiangya, the court was divided. Explain your thinking to me."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「此乃致敵上策，恨未能，多爾。

translations.literal: He replied: "This was precisely the superior stratagem for bringing the enemy in; I regret only that we could not do more of it.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "That was the best way to draw the enemy in. I only regret that we could not do more of it.

sentences.zh: 並邊生羌善馳突，識鄉導，儻能撫柔之，所謂以外夷而攻外夷也。」

translations.literal: The raw Qiang along the border excel at rapid raids and know the guides; if they could be placated and treated gently, it is what is called using outer tribes to attack outer tribes."
translations.idiomatic: The raw Qiang along the border excel at swift raids and know every path. If they can be won over and treated kindly, that is what is meant by using one outer people to strike another."

sentences.zh: 帝於是決意招納，多獲其用。

translations.literal: The emperor then resolved on recruitment and frequently gained their service.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then resolved to pursue such recruitment and often profited from it.

sentences.zh: 知文郁善左射，並招其子弟閱肄殿庭，文鬱九發八中，詔官其二子。

translations.literal: Learning Wenyu was skilled at left-handed shooting, he also summoned his sons and nephews to drill in the palace courtyard; Wenyu hit eight of nine shots; an edict enfeoffed two of his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Wenyu was a skilled left-handed archer, the emperor also summoned his sons and nephews to drill in the palace courtyard. Wenyu hit eight of nine shots, and an edict granted office to two of his sons.

sentences.zh: 知鎮戎、德順軍，預定洮、河，遷左騏驥副使、知麟州。

translations.literal: He administered Zhenrong and Deshun armies, participated in fixing Tao and He, was transferred to Left Qilin Vice Commissioner and Administrator of Lin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Zhenrong and Deshun armies, took part in securing the Tao and He regions, and was promoted to Left Qilin Vice Commissioner and prefect of Lin.

sentences.zh: 夏眾踐稼，襲敗之，部使者劾為生事，奪郡印。

translations.literal: Xia masses trampled the crops; he raided and defeated them; the circuit inspector impeached him for provocation and stripped his prefectural seal.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia troops trampled the crops, he struck and defeated them, but a circuit inspector impeached him for provoking trouble and stripped him of his prefectural seal.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為熙河將。

translations.literal: Before long, he became a Xihe general.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made a general on the Xihe frontier.

sentences.zh: 李憲討靈武，文鬱得羌戶萬余，遷路鈐轄。

translations.literal: Li Xian campaigned against Lingwu; Wenyu obtained more than ten thousand Qiang households; he was transferred to Circuit Controller.
translations.idiomatic: On Li Xian's campaign against Lingwu, Wenyu brought over more than ten thousand Qiang households and was promoted to circuit controller.

sentences.zh: 夏人圍蘭州，已奪兩關門，文鬱募死士夜縋而下，持短兵突賊，即掃營去。

translations.literal: The Xia besieged Lanzhou, having already taken two gate towers; Wenyu recruited dare-to-die soldiers who were lowered by rope at night, seized short weapons and burst into the enemy camp, then swept the camp and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xia besieged Lan Prefecture and had already seized two gate towers, Wenyu recruited dare-to-die troops who were lowered by rope at night, seized short weapons, burst into the enemy camp, and then swept it clean before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 擢東上閣門使、知蘭州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner and Administrator of Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner and put in charge of Lan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 諜知夏人將大入，清野以俟，果舉國趨皋蘭，文鬱乘城禦之，殺傷如積，圍九日而解，收其屍為京觀，加榮州團練使，以捧日、天武都指揮使為副都總管，以殿前都虞候知河州。

translations.literal: Spies reported the Xia were about to invade in force; he stripped the countryside and waited; indeed the whole state marched toward Gaolan; Wenyu manned the walls to resist; casualties piled up; the siege was lifted after nine days; he collected their corpses into a victory mound; he was additionally made Regimental Commissioner of Rongzhou; as Commander of the Pengri and Tianwu commands he served as Deputy Overall Commander; as Palace Front Command Vice Commissioner he administered Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Spies reported that the Xia were about to invade in force. He cleared the countryside and waited, and indeed the whole Xia state marched on Gaolan. Wenyu held the walls and fought them off until casualties lay in heaps. After nine days the siege was lifted. He piled the enemy dead into a victory mound, was additionally made Regimental Commissioner of Rongzhou, appointed deputy overall commander with command of the Pengri and Tianwu guards, and made Palace Front Command Vice Commissioner and prefect of He.

sentences.zh: 築安西城、金城關，進秦州防禦、冀州觀察使。

translations.literal: He built Anxi city and Jincheng Pass; he was promoted to Defense Commissioner of Qinzhou and Observation Commissioner of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He built Anxi city and Jincheng Pass and was promoted to Defense Commissioner of Qin and Observation Commissioner of Ji.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: He died, age sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 周永清

translations.literal: Zhou Yongqing
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yongqing

sentences.zh: 周永清字肅之。

translations.literal: Zhou Yongqing, style name Suzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yongqing, courtesy name Suzhi.

sentences.zh: 世家靈州，州陷，祖美歸京師。

translations.literal: His family had long lived in Lingzhou; when the prefecture fell, his grandfather Mei returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long been established in Ling Prefecture. When the prefecture fell, his grandfather Mei returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 永清以蔭從仕，宰相寵籍言其忠勇，加閣門祗候。

translations.literal: Yongqing entered service through yin privilege; the chancellor Pang Ji spoke of his loyalty and courage; he was added as Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yongqing entered office through hereditary privilege. The chief councilor Pang Ji spoke of his loyalty and courage, and he was promoted to Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 押時服賜夏國，至宥州，夏人受賜不跪，詰之，恐而跪。

translations.literal: Escorting seasonal gifts to the Xia state, at Youzhou the Xia received the gifts without kneeling; he interrogated them; in fear they knelt.
translations.idiomatic: While escorting seasonal gifts to the Xia state, he reached You Prefecture, where the Xia received the gifts without kneeling. He rebuked them, and in fear they knelt.

sentences.zh: 遷通事舍人、渭州鈐轄。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant at the Office of Transmission Affairs and Weizhou Circuit Controller.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant at the Office of Transmission Affairs and controller of Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 渭兵勁而陳伍不講，永清訓以李靖法。

translations.literal: Weizhou troops were strong but their formations and ranks were not drilled; Yongqing trained them by Li Jing's methods.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei troops were fierce but their formations were undisciplined, so Yongqing drilled them according to Li Jing's methods.

sentences.zh: 帥蔡挺嘉其整，圖上之，詔推于諸道。

translations.literal: Commander Cai Ting praised his orderliness, submitted diagrams to the throne; an edict extended it to all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: The commander Cai Ting praised his discipline, submitted diagrams to the throne, and an edict ordered the method spread to every circuit.

sentences.zh: 知德順軍，夏眾入寇，擊擒其酋呂效忠。

translations.literal: Administering Deshun Army, when Xia masses entered raiding he struck and captured their chieftain Lü Xiaozhong.
translations.idiomatic: As commander of Deshun Army, when Xia forces raided the frontier he attacked and captured their chieftain Lü Xiaozhong.

sentences.zh: 又募勇士夜馳百里，搗賊巢穴，斬首三百級，俘數千人，獲橐駝、甲馬萬計。

translations.literal: He also recruited brave men who rode a hundred li by night, stormed the bandits' nest, beheaded three hundred, captured several thousand, and seized camels, armor, and horses beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: He also recruited brave men who rode a hundred li by night, struck the enemy nest, took three hundred heads, captured several thousand men, and seized camels, armor, and horses by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 城中無知者。

translations.literal: Those in the city knew nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: Those in the city knew nothing of the raid until it was over.

sentences.zh: 並砦禁地三百里，盜耕不可禁，永清拓籍數千頃，置射士二千，聲聞敵廷。

translations.literal: Along the border forts, forbidden land three hundred li—illicit cultivation could not be stopped; Yongqing expanded registration by several thousand qing, posted two thousand archers; his fame reached the enemy court.
translations.idiomatic: For three hundred li around the border forts, forbidden land was illegally farmed and could not be stopped. Yongqing expanded the registered domain by several thousand qing, posted two thousand archers, and his reputation reached the enemy court.

sentences.zh: 降者引入帳下，待之不疑。

translations.literal: Surrenderers he brought under his tent and treated them without suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: He brought surrenderers into his own tent and treated them without suspicion.

sentences.zh: 多得其死力。

translations.literal: Many gave him their utmost loyalty in return.
translations.idiomatic: Many repaid him with their utmost loyalty.

sentences.zh: 徙秦鳳鈐轄、河北沿邊安撫副使、知代州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Qin-Feng Circuit Controller, Deputy Frontier Pacification Commissioner of Hebei, and Administrator of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to controller of the Qin-Feng circuit, deputy frontier pacification commissioner of Hebei, and prefect of Dai.

sentences.zh: 契丹無名求地，朝廷命韓縝分畫，永清貳焉，入對言：「疆境不可輕與人，臣職守土，不願行。」

translations.literal: The Khitan sought land without clear pretext; the court ordered Han Zhen to demarcate; Yongqing was assigned as second [commissioner]; entering audience he said: "Territory must not be lightly given away; my duty is to guard the soil—I do not wish to go.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan demanded land without clear cause, the court ordered Han Zhen to demarcate the border and assigned Yongqing as his second. Appearing before the emperor he said, "Territory must not be lightly surrendered. My duty is to guard the land, and I do not wish to go.

sentences.zh: 固遣之，復上章陳利害，竟以母病辭。

translations.literal: [The emperor] nevertheless sent him; he again submitted a memorial setting forth advantages and disadvantages, and in the end declined on grounds of his mother's illness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent him anyway. He submitted another memorial explaining the advantages and disadvantages, and in the end declined on the grounds of his mother's illness.

sentences.zh: 曆高陽關、定州、涇原路鈐轄，知涇州、保州，又為定州路副總管，終東上閣門使。

translations.literal: He served successively as Controller of Gaoyang Pass, Dingzhou, and Jingyuan Circuit; Administrator of Jingzhou and Baozhou; also Deputy Commander-in-chief of Dingzhou Circuit; and ended as Attendant on the Eastern Upper Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as controller of Gaoyang Pass, Ding Prefecture, and the Jingyuan circuit, as prefect of Jing and Bao, and as deputy commander-in-chief of the Ding circuit, and ended his career as Attendant on the Eastern Upper Gate.

sentences.zh: 劉紹能

translations.literal: Liu Shaoneng
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shaoneng

sentences.zh: 劉紹能字及之，保安軍人。

translations.literal: Liu Shaoneng, courtesy name Jizhi, was a native of Bao'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shaoneng, courtesy name Jizhi, was from Bao'an Army.

sentences.zh: 世為諸族巡檢，父懷忠，官內殿崇班、閣門祗候。

translations.literal: For generations [the family] served as inspectors of the various tribes; his father Huai Zhong held the posts of Inner Hall Honorary Companion and Attendant at the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family had served as inspectors of the frontier tribes. His father, Huai Zhong, held the posts of Inner Hall Honorary Companion and Attendant at the Gate.

sentences.zh: 元昊叛，厚以金幣及王爵招之，懷忠毀印斬使，洎入寇，力戰以死。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao rebelled, he lavishly offered gold, silks, and a princely title to win him over; Huai Zhong destroyed the seal and beheaded the envoy; when [the Xia] subsequently invaded, he fought fiercely and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao rebelled, he tried to win Huai Zhong over with lavish gifts of gold and silk and the offer of a princely title. Huai Zhong destroyed the seal and beheaded the envoy. When the Xia subsequently invaded, he fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 錄紹能右班殿直，賜以名，為軍北巡檢。

translations.literal: Shaoneng was enrolled as Right Squad Palace Guard and granted the imperial surname; he was made Northern Inspector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoneng was enrolled in office as Right Squad Palace Guard and granted the imperial surname; he was appointed northern frontier inspector of the army.

sentences.zh: 擊破夏右樞密院黨移賞糧數萬眾于順寧。

translations.literal: At Shunning he defeated tens of thousands under Dang Yishaliang of the Xia Right Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: At Shunning he routed tens of thousands of troops under Dang Yishaliang of the Xia Right Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 夏人圍大順城，紹能為軍鋒，毀其柵，至奈王川，邀擊于長城嶺，熙寧中，又敗夏人於破囉川，皆策功最。

translations.literal: When Xia forces besieged Dashun City, Shaoneng served as vanguard, destroyed their palisade, reached Naiwang River; he ambushed them at Changcheng Ridge; in the Xining era he again defeated Xia forces at Poluo River—all with foremost merit in the reports.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia forces besieged Dashun City, Shaoneng led the vanguard, destroyed their palisades, and pushed as far as Naiwang River; he ambushed the enemy at Changcheng Ridge. In the Xining reign he again defeated Xia forces at Poluo River, and in each case his merit was ranked first.

sentences.zh: 累遷洛苑使、英州刺史、鄜延兵馬都監。

translations.literal: He was promoted successively to Luoyuan Commissioner, Prefect of Yingzhou, and Chief Inspector of Military Affairs in Fuyan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Luoyuan Commissioner, prefect of Ying, and chief military inspector of Fuyan.

sentences.zh: 舊制，內屬者不與漢官齒，至是，悉如之，仍以其子襲故職。

translations.literal: Under old regulations, inner subordinates were not ranked on equal footing with Han officials; at this time all were treated alike, and moreover his son inherited his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old regulations, frontier subjects who had come under imperial authority were not ranked on equal footing with Han officials. Now they were all treated alike, and his son was allowed to inherit his former post.

sentences.zh: 元豐西討，召詣闕，神宗訪以計，對曰：「師旅遠征，儲偫不繼為大患。

translations.literal: During the Yuanfeng western campaign, he was summoned to court; Emperor Shenzong consulted him on strategy; he replied: "When troops march far on campaign, the failure of provisions and stores to keep up is the greatest calamity.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfeng western expedition he was summoned to court. Emperor Shenzong asked his advice on strategy, and he replied, "On a distant campaign, the greatest danger is when supplies run out and cannot keep pace with the army.

sentences.zh: 若俟西成後，因糧深入，乃可以得志。」

translations.literal: If one waits until the western harvest is complete and advances deep relying on grain, then one may achieve one's aim.
translations.idiomatic: If we wait until the western harvest is in and then advance deep into enemy territory, relying on local grain, we can achieve our objective.

sentences.zh: 帝以為然，命統兩軍進討。

translations.literal: The emperor approved, and ordered him to command both armies in the advance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and ordered him to command both armies in the advance.

sentences.zh: 紹能世世邊將，為敵所忌，每設疑以間之。

translations.literal: Shaoneng's family for generations had been frontier generals; the enemy envied them and constantly sowed suspicion to drive a wedge.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the Shaoneng family had served as frontier generals, and the enemy feared them. They repeatedly planted suspicion in hopes of driving a wedge between Shaoneng and the court.

sentences.zh: 帝獨明其不然，手詔云：「紹能戰功最多，忠勇第一，此必夏人畏忌，為間害之計耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor alone saw through this; he personally wrote: "Shaoneng's battle merit is the greatest, his loyalty and valor foremost—this must be the Xia people's fear and envy, a stratagem to harm him through suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor alone saw through this and wrote in his own hand: "Shaoneng's battle merit is the greatest and his loyalty and courage unmatched. This rumor must be the work of the Xia, who fear him and seek to destroy him through suspicion.

sentences.zh: 紹能捧詔感泣。

translations.literal: Shaoneng received the edict in both hands and wept with emotion.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoneng received the edict with both hands and wept.

sentences.zh: 嘗坐讒逮對，按驗卒無實。

translations.literal: He once was implicated by slander and arrested for interrogation; investigation ultimately found no substance.
translations.idiomatic: He was once implicated by slander and summoned for interrogation, but investigation found no substance to the charges.

sentences.zh: 守邊圉四十七年，大小五十戰，以皇城使、簡州團練使卒。

translations.literal: He guarded the frontier forty-seven years, fought fifty battles large and small, and died holding the posts of Imperial City Commissioner and Regimented Militia Commissioner of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He defended the frontier for forty-seven years and fought fifty engagements, large and small. He died while serving as Imperial City Commissioner and regimented militia commissioner of Jian.

sentences.zh: 王光祖

translations.literal: Wang Guangzu
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guangzu

sentences.zh: 王光祖，字君俞，開封人。

translations.literal: Wang Guangzu, courtesy name Junyu, was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guangzu, courtesy name Junyu, was from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父珪，為涇原勇將，號「王鐵鞭」，戰死好水川。

translations.literal: His father Gui was a brave general of Jingyuan, known as "Wang Iron Whip"; he died in battle at Haoshui River.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gui was a fierce general of Jingyuan known as "Iron Whip Wang"; he was killed in battle at Haoshui River.

sentences.zh: 錄光祖為供奉官、閣門祗候。

translations.literal: Guangzu was enrolled as Attendant-official and Attendant at the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzu was enrolled in office as Attendant-official and Attendant at the Gate in recognition of his father's service.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，同提點河北刑獄，改沿邊安撫都監，進副使。

translations.literal: In the Xining era he served as Co-intendant of Hebei Judicial Affairs; was transferred to Chief Inspector of Frontier Pacification; was promoted to Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining reign he served as co-intendant of Hebei judicial affairs, then was transferred to chief inspector of frontier pacification and promoted to vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 界河巡檢趙用擾北邊，契丹以兵數萬壓境，造浮橋，如欲度者。

translations.literal: Border-river inspector Zhao Yong disturbed the northern frontier; the Khitan brought tens of thousands of troops to press the border, built pontoon bridges, as if preparing to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yong, the border-river inspector, was causing trouble on the northern frontier. The Khitan mobilized tens of thousands of troops along the border, built pontoon bridges, and appeared ready to cross.

sentences.zh: 光祖在舟中，對其眾盡徹戶牖。

translations.literal: Guangzu was aboard a boat; facing their masses he completely removed doors and windows.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzu was aboard his boat; facing the Khitan army, he had every door and window removed from the vessel.

sentences.zh: 或謂：「契丹方陣，而以單舟臨之，如不測何？」

translations.literal: Someone said: "The Khitan are in full battle array, yet you approach with a single boat—what if something unforeseen happens?
