translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "The Khitan are in full battle formation, and you are approaching in a single boat. What if something goes wrong?

sentences.zh: 光祖曰：「彼所顧者，信誓也；

translations.literal: Guangzu said: "What they care about is sworn faith;
translations.idiomatic: Guangzu replied, "What they care about is the sworn faith between our states;

sentences.zh: 其來，欲得趙用耳。

translations.literal: their coming is only to get Zhao Yong.
translations.idiomatic: They have come only to get Zhao Yong.

sentences.zh: 避之則勢張，吾死不足塞責。」

translations.literal: If we avoid them their momentum will swell; my death would not suffice to answer for the responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: If we avoid them their pressure will only grow. My death alone would not be enough to answer for this responsibility.

sentences.zh: 已而契丹欲相與言，光祖即命子襄往。

translations.literal: Before long the Khitan wished to speak together; Guangzu immediately ordered his son Xiang to go.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Khitan asked to parley. Guangzu at once sent his son Xiang.

sentences.zh: 兵刃四合，然語唯在用，襄隨機折塞之。

translations.literal: Weapons closed in on all sides, yet the talk concerned only Yong; Xiang parried and blocked as occasion demanded.
translations.idiomatic: Blades surrounded him on every side, but the talks concerned only Zhao Yong, and Xiang parried each demand as it came.

sentences.zh: 其將蕭禧遽揮兵去，且邀襄食，付所戴青羅泥金笠以為信，即上之。

translations.literal: Their general Xiao Xi abruptly waved his troops away, moreover invited Xiang to dine, and gave the green-silk, gold-flecked hat he wore as token of trust; [Xiang] immediately presented it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan general Xiao Xi abruptly withdrew his troops, invited Xiang to a meal, and gave him the green silk hat flecked with gold mud that he was wearing as a token of good faith. Xiang at once presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 時已有詔罷光祖矣。

translations.literal: By then an edict had already removed Guangzu from office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict removing Guangzu from office had already been issued.

sentences.zh: 吳充曰：「向非光祖以身對壘，又使子冒白刃取從約，則事未可知。

translations.literal: Wu Chong said: "Had it not been for Guangzu facing the enemy ramparts in person, and sending his son to brave bare blades and secure a compact, the outcome would have been unpredictable.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chong said, "Had Guangzu not faced the enemy in person and sent his son through drawn blades to secure agreement, the outcome might have been disastrous.

sentences.zh: 宜賞而黜，何以示懲勸？」

translations.literal: He should be rewarded yet was dismissed—how does this show encouragement and warning?
translations.idiomatic: To reward merit with dismissal—what sort of message does that send about encouragement and punishment?

sentences.zh: 乃除真定鈐轄。

translations.literal: [The emperor] thereupon appointed him Controller of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzu was then appointed controller of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 徙梓夔。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Zikui [circuit].
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Zikui region.

sentences.zh: 渝獠叛，詔熊本安撫，而命內藏庫使楊萬、成都鈐轄賈昌言、梓夔都監王宣與光祖同致討，皆受本節度。

translations.literal: When the Yu Liao rebelled, an edict made Xiong Ben pacification commissioner; and ordered Inner Treasury Commissioner Yang Wan, Chengdu Controller Jia Changyan, Zikui Chief Inspector Wang Xuan, and Guangzu jointly to mount a punitive campaign—all under Ben's command.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao of Yu rebelled, the court appointed Xiong Ben pacification commissioner and ordered Inner Treasury Commissioner Yang Wan, Chengdu controller Jia Changyan, Zikui chief inspector Wang Xuan, and Guangzu to join in the punitive campaign, all under Ben's command.

sentences.zh: 本疑光祖不為用，分三道進師，使光祖將後軍，出黃沙坎。

translations.literal: Ben doubted Guangzu would obey; he divided the army into three routes; he had Guangzu lead the rear army, exiting via Huangsha Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Ben doubted that Guangzu would follow orders. He divided the force into three columns and assigned Guangzu the rear column, sent out through Huangsha Pass.

sentences.zh: 比發，日已暮，士以杖索塗，相挽而前，夜半，抵絕頂。

translations.literal: By the time they set out the sun had set; soldiers used staffs to feel the path, helping one another forward; at midnight they reached the summit.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they set out, dusk had fallen. The men used staffs to feel their way along the trail, pulling one another forward, and by midnight they had reached the summit.

sentences.zh: 質明，獠望見，大駭，一鼓而潰。

translations.literal: At dawn the Liao saw them, were greatly terrified, and dispersed at the first drumroll.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the rebels saw them, were terrified, and broke at the first drumbeat.

sentences.zh: 萬等困於松谿，又亟往援。

translations.literal: Wan and the others were trapped at Songxi; [Guangzu] again hastened to their relief.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wan and his force were pinned down at Song Creek, and Guangzu hurried to their relief.

sentences.zh: 出石門，敓其險，促黔兵先登襲賊，賊舍去。

translations.literal: Exiting Shimen Pass he seized their strong point, urged Qian troops to ascend first and strike the bandits; the bandits abandoned [the position].
translations.idiomatic: He pushed through Shimen Pass, seized the high ground, and sent Qian troops up first to strike the rebels, who abandoned their positions.

sentences.zh: 光祖夜泊松嶺上，旦始遇萬等，與俱還。

translations.literal: Guangzu anchored overnight on Song Ridge; at dawn he finally met Wan and the others, and returned together.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzu camped overnight on Song Ridge and did not meet Wan's force until dawn, after which they returned together.

sentences.zh: 本愧謝，上其功第一。

translations.literal: Ben apologized in shame and reported his merit as foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Ben apologized and submitted a report ranking Guangzu's merit first.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃圍茂州，光祖領兵三千，會王中正破雞宗關，賊據石鼓村，扼其半道。

translations.literal: When Tibetans besieged Maozhou, Guangzu led three thousand troops; joining Wang Zhongzheng who broke Jizong Pass, the bandits held Shigu Village, blocking half the route.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans besieged Maozhou, Guangzu led three thousand troops. Wang Zhongzheng had broken through Jizong Pass, but the enemy held Shigu Village and blocked the mid-route.

sentences.zh: 中正召諸將問計，光祖獨請行。

translations.literal: Zhongzheng summoned the generals to ask for plans; Guangzu alone requested to go.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzheng summoned the generals for counsel; Guangzu alone volunteered to go.

sentences.zh: 既抵石鼓，擇銳兵分襲吐蕃背，出其不意，皆驚遁，遂會中正於茂。

translations.literal: Having reached Shigu, he selected elite troops to divide and strike the Tibetans' rear; taking them unawares, all fled in panic; he then joined Zhongzheng at Mao[zhou].
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Shigu, he chose elite troops for a divided strike on the Tibetan rear. Caught by surprise, the enemy fled in panic, and Guangzu joined Zhongzheng at Maozhou.

sentences.zh: 瀘夷乞弟殺王宣，詔從韓存寶討之，軍于梅嶺。

translations.literal: The Lu Yi chieftain Qidi killed Wang Xuan; an edict ordered [Guangzu] to follow Han Cunbao in punitive action; the army encamped at Meiling.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu tribal leader Qidi killed Wang Xuan. An edict ordered Guangzu to join Han Cunbao in a punitive expedition, and the army encamped at Meiling.

sentences.zh: 夷數萬眾出駐落個棧，欲老我師。

translations.literal: The Yi mustered tens of thousands at Luoge Stack, intending to wear down our army.
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen mustered tens of thousands at Luoge Stack, intending to wear down the Song army.

sentences.zh: 霖雨不止，光祖勸存寶早決戰。

translations.literal: Continuous rains would not stop; Guangzu urged Cunbao to decide battle early.
translations.idiomatic: The rains would not let up, and Guangzu urged Cunbao to commit to battle soon.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: [Cunbao] would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Cunbao refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 林廣至，復從征，蕩其巢窟。

translations.literal: When Lin Guang arrived, [Guangzu] again followed on campaign and swept their nests clean.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Guang arrived, Guangzu joined the campaign again and swept their strongholds clean.

sentences.zh: 積功至四方館使、知瀘州。

translations.literal: Accumulating merit he reached the post of Commissioner of the Four Directions Hall and Administrator of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Through accumulated merit he rose to Commissioner of the Four Directions Hall and prefect of Lu.

sentences.zh: 置瀘南安撫使，俾兼領，邊事聽顓決。

translations.literal: The Luzhou Southern Pacification Commissioner was established; he was made to hold it concurrently; frontier affairs were entrusted to his sole decision.
translations.idiomatic: When the post of Southern Pacification Commissioner of Lu was established, he was given it concurrently, with sole authority over frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 遷客省使、嘉州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Office of Guests and Prefect of Jiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commissioner of the Office of Guests and prefect of Jia.

sentences.zh: 曆涇原、河東、定州路副總管，卒。

translations.literal: He served successively as Deputy Commander-in-chief of Jingyuan, Hedong, and Dingzhou Circuits; he died.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as deputy commander-in-chief of the Jingyuan, Hedong, and Ding circuits, then died.

sentences.zh: 李浩，字直夫，家本綏州，徙西河。

translations.literal: Li Hao, courtesy name Zhifu; his family was originally from Suizhou, later moved to Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hao, courtesy name Zhifu, came from a family originally of Suizhou that had moved to Xihe.

sentences.zh: 浩務學，通兵法，以父定蔭，從軍破儂智高。

translations.literal: Hao applied himself to study, mastered military methods; through his father Ding's yin privilege he joined the army and helped defeat Nong Zhigao.
translations.idiomatic: Hao devoted himself to study and mastered military science. Through his father Ding's privilege of inherited appointment he joined the army and helped defeat Nong Zhigao.

sentences.zh: 韓絳城囉兀，領兵戰賞堡嶺川，殺大首領訛革多移，斬首千三百餘級。

translations.literal: When Han Jiang fortified Luowu, [Hao] led troops and fought at Shangbao Lingchuan, killing the great chieftain E Geduoyi; heads taken exceeded thirteen hundred.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Jiang fortified Luowu, Hao led troops in battle at Shangbao Lingchuan, killed the great chieftain E Geduoyi, and took more than thirteen hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 積官供備庫副使、廣西都監。

translations.literal: Accumulating offices he reached Deputy Commissioner of the Prepared Stores Bureau and Chief Inspector of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to deputy commissioner of the Prepared Stores Bureau and chief military inspector of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 裒西北疆事著《安邊策》，謁王安石。

translations.literal: He collected northwest frontier affairs and wrote "Policies for Securing the Border"; he called on Wang Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled his knowledge of northwest frontier affairs into Policies for Securing the Border and presented himself to Wang Anshi.

sentences.zh: 安石言之神宗，召對，改管幹麟府兵馬。

translations.literal: Anshi spoke of him to Emperor Shenzong; [Hao] was summoned for audience and was changed to Director-in-chief of Lin-Fu Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi recommended him to Emperor Shenzong. Hao was summoned to audience and appointed director-in-chief of Lin-Fu military affairs.

sentences.zh: 未行，又從章惇于南江，引兵由三路屯鎮江，入遂州，討舒光貴，破盈口柵，下天府，會於洽州，入懿州。

translations.literal: Before departing, he again followed Zhang Dun at Nanjiang; leading troops by three routes he garrisoned Zhenjiang, entered Suizhou, campaigned against Shu Guanggui, broke Yingkou Palisade, took Tianfu, assembled at Qiazhou, and entered Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart he was sent again with Zhang Dun to Nanjiang. He led troops along three routes, garrisoned Zhenjiang, entered Suizhou, and campaigned against Shu Guanggui. He broke through Yingkou Palisade, took Tianfu, rendezvoused at Qia, and pushed into Yi.

sentences.zh: 蠻酋田元猛、元哲合狤狑拒官軍，浩分兵擊之，殺狤狑，降元猛、元哲，遂城懿州。

translations.literal: Man chieftains Tian Yuanmeng and Yuanzhe joined Jiji to resist the official army; Hao divided troops to strike them, killed Jiji, accepted the surrender of Yuanmeng and Yuanzhe, and then fortified Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal chieftains Tian Yuanmeng and Yuanzhe joined with Jiji to resist the imperial army. Hao divided his force, killed Jiji, received the surrender of Yuanmeng and Yuanzhe, and then fortified Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 進討黔江蠻，復城黔江。

translations.literal: Advancing to campaign against Qianjiang Man, he restored Qianjiang city.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing against the Qianjiang tribes, he recovered and rebuilt Qianjiang.

sentences.zh: 惇上其功，謂不當與他將比，擢引進副使、熙河鈐轄。

translations.literal: Dun reported his merit, saying he should not be compared with other generals; [Hao] was promoted to Vice Introducer and Controller of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun submitted a report on his merit, arguing that he should not be ranked alongside ordinary generals. Hao was promoted to Vice Introducer and controller of the Xihe circuit.

sentences.zh: 李憲討山后羌，浩將右軍至合龍嶺會戰，遣降羌乞嘊輕騎突敵帳，俘其酋冷雞朴、李密撒，馘三千。

translations.literal: When Li Xian campaigned against the Shanhou Qiang, Hao led the right army to join battle at Helong Ridge; he dispatched the surrendered Qiang Qi'ai with light cavalry to burst into the enemy encampment, capturing chieftains Leng Jipu and Li Misa; heads taken: three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xian campaigned against the Shanhou Qiang, Hao led the right wing to battle at Helong Ridge. He sent the surrendered Qiang Qi'ai with light cavalry to burst into the enemy camp, captured the chieftains Leng Jipu and Li Misa, and took three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 遷東上閣門使，為副總管、知河州、安撫洮西。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant on the Eastern Upper Gate; made Deputy Commander-in-chief, Administrator of Hezhou, and Pacification Commissioner of Taoxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant on the Eastern Upper Gate, appointed deputy commander-in-chief, prefect of He, and pacification commissioner of the Taoxi region.

sentences.zh: 五路大舉，浩將前軍，復蘭州。

translations.literal: In the five-route grand offensive, Hao led the vanguard and recovered Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the five-route grand offensive, Hao led the vanguard and recaptured Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷引進使、隴州防禦使、知蘭州兼熙河、涇原安撫副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Introducer, Defense Commissioner of Longzhou, Administrator of Lanzhou and concurrently Deputy Pacification Commissioner of Xihe and Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Introducer and defense commissioner of Long, given Lan Prefecture with concurrent posts as deputy pacification commissioner for the Xihe and Jingyuan circuits.

sentences.zh: 坐西關失守及報上不實，再貶秩。

translations.literal: On account of the loss of Xiguan and reporting to the throne that was not truthful, he was demoted in rank twice.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted twice for the loss of Xiguan and for making false reports to the throne.

sentences.zh: 旋以戰吃囉、瓦井連立功，復之。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, through merit in battles at Chiluo and Wajing in succession, [his rank] was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, through successive victories at Chiluo and Wajing, his rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 哲宗即位，拜忠州防禦使、捧日天武都指揮使、馬軍都虞候，進黔州觀察使，曆鄜延、太原、永興、環慶路副都總管，再知蘭州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong acceded, [Hao] was appointed Defense Commissioner of Zhongzhou, Commander of the Pons Day Heavenly Martial [Guard], Deputy Commander of the Horse Army; promoted to Observation Commissioner of Qianzhou; served successively as Deputy Overall Commander of Fuyan, Taiyuan, Yongxing, and Huanqing Circuits; again Administrator of Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, Hao was appointed defense commissioner of Zhong, commander of the Pons Day Heavenly Martial Guard, and deputy commander of the horse army; promoted to observation commissioner of Qian; served successively as deputy overall commander of the Fuyan, Taiyuan, Yongxing, and Huanqing circuits; and again became prefect of Lan.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈安化軍留後。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted Military Commissioner of Anhua Army.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the title of military commissioner of Anhua.

sentences.zh: 和斌，字勝之，濮州鄄城人。

translations.literal: He Bin, courtesy name Shengzhi, was a native of Juancheng in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Bin, courtesy name Shengzhi, was from Juancheng in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 選隸散直，為德順軍指揮使，凡五年，數捍敵，被重創十餘。

translations.literal: Selected for the Scattered Direct [Guard], he was Deshun Army Commander; in all five years he repeatedly repelled the enemy and received serious wounds more than ten times.
translations.idiomatic: After selection for the Scattered Direct Guard he became commander of Deshun Army. Over five years he repeatedly repelled the enemy and suffered more than ten serious wounds.

sentences.zh: 知軍事劉兼濟以兄平敗沒，執送京師，並逮其家。

translations.literal: Military administrator Liu Jianji, because his elder brother Ping was defeated and lost, was arrested and sent to the capital; his family was also seized.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jianji, the military administrator, was arrested and sent to the capital because his elder brother Ping had been defeated and killed; his whole family was taken into custody as well.

sentences.zh: 斌慰安調護，為寓金帛他所，密告兼濟勿以家為恤。

translations.literal: Bin comforted and looked after him, lodged gold and silks elsewhere, and secretly told Jianji not to worry about his family.
translations.idiomatic: Bin comforted and cared for him, hid gold and silk elsewhere, and secretly told Jianji not to worry about his family.

sentences.zh: 平冤既伸，兼濟獲免，家賴以全。

translations.literal: Once Ping's injustice was redressed, Jianji was spared; the family relied on this to be preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: When Ping's name was cleared, Jianji was spared, and his family was preserved intact.

sentences.zh: 定川之役，將曹偀喪所乘馬，斌輟騎與之，且戰且行，與俱免。

translations.literal: At the battle of Dingchuan, General Cao Ying lost the horse he rode; Bin gave up his own mount to him; fighting as they went, both escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Dingchuan, General Cao Ying lost his mount. Bin gave him his own horse, and fighting as they withdrew, both escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 狄青南征，使部騎兵為前鋒。

translations.literal: When Di Qing campaigned south, [Bin] was made to command cavalry as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: On Di Qing's southern expedition, Bin commanded the cavalry vanguard.

sentences.zh: 青駐賓州十日以怠寇，既乃倍道兼行。

translations.literal: Qing halted at Binzhou ten days to weary the bandits; then he doubled the marching pace.
translations.idiomatic: Qing held at Binzhou for ten days to lull the enemy, then marched at double speed.

sentences.zh: 斌以兵疲於險，利在速戰，即日度關。

translations.literal: Bin, seeing the troops weary on dangerous terrain, judged that advantage lay in swift battle; that same day they crossed the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Bin saw that the troops were exhausted on difficult terrain and that speed was essential. That same day they crossed the pass.

sentences.zh: 鏖賊歸仁驛，孫節死，斌引騎血戰，繞出賊後，遂敗之。

translations.literal: Fierce battle at Guiren Post; Sun Jie died; Bin led cavalry in bloody combat, swung around behind the bandits, and thus defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At Guiren Post they fought a fierce engagement in which Sun Jie was killed. Bin led his cavalry through bloody combat, swung around behind the enemy, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 師還，張破賊陳形於殿廷，仁宗拊勞，擢文思副使、權廣西鈐轄。

translations.literal: When the army returned, [Di Qing] displayed diagrams of the broken enemy formation in the palace hall; Emperor Renzong clapped his shoulder in praise; [Bin] was promoted to Vice Commissioner of Literary Endeavor and Acting Controller of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Di Qing displayed diagrams of the broken enemy formation in the palace hall. Emperor Renzong personally commended him and promoted Bin to Vice Commissioner of Literary Endeavor and acting controller of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 改秦鳳，廣西以蠻事乞留，秦州亦請之，詔留廣西。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Qin-Feng; Guangxi pleaded to retain him on account of barbarian affairs; Qinzhou also requested him; an edict kept him in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Qin-Feng, but Guangxi petitioned to keep him because of tribal unrest, and Qin Prefecture petitioned for him as well. An edict ordered him to remain in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 累歲，徙涇原。

translations.literal: After several years he was transferred to Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he was transferred to Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 召對，議者謂交州可取，斌盛言有害無益，願戒邊臣無妄動。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, when discussants said Jiaozhou could be taken, Bin strongly argued harm without benefit, wishing to admonish frontier officials not to act rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to audience, he heard officials argue that Jiaozhi could be taken. Bin argued forcefully that the venture would do more harm than good and urged the emperor to warn frontier officials against rash action.

sentences.zh: 神宗歎曰：「卿質直如此，乃知兩路爭卿，為不誣矣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong sighed: "Your forthrightness is such as this—now I know the two circuits' competing for you was no false report.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong sighed and said, "With such plainspoken integrity as yours, no wonder both circuits were competing for your services.

sentences.zh: 進帶禦器械。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Bearer of Imperial Ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Bearer of Imperial Ordinance.

sentences.zh: 渭部饑，帥王廣淵命吏賑給，斌曰：「救之無術，是殺之耳。」

translations.literal: When Wei circuit suffered famine, Commander Wang Guangyuan ordered clerks to distribute relief; Bin said: "To relieve without method is simply to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck Wei, the commander Wang Guangyuan ordered clerks to distribute relief. Bin said, "Relief without a proper plan is no better than killing them outright.

sentences.zh: 廣淵以委斌，斌擇地營居，養視有法，所活以萬數。

translations.literal: Guangyuan entrusted it to Bin; Bin chose land and set up camps, nursed and cared with method; those saved numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan put the task in Bin's hands. Bin chose sites, organized camps, and administered relief with proper method, saving tens of thousands of lives.

sentences.zh: 安南入寇，復徙廣西。

translations.literal: When Annam invaded, he was again transferred to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Annam invaded, he was transferred back to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 累遷皇城使、昭州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted successively to Imperial City Commissioner and Prefect of Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Imperial City Commissioner and prefect of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 撫水蠻羅世念犯宜州，守將戰死。

translations.literal: The Fushui Man chieftain Luo Shinan attacked Yizhou; the defending general died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shinan of the Fushui tribes attacked Yizhou, and the defending general was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 斌提步騎三千進討，方暑，晝夜趣兵，至懷遠寨，曰：「此要害之地，得之則生。」

translations.literal: Bin led three thousand infantry and cavalry on punitive advance; in the heat of summer he rushed troops day and night; reaching Huaiyuan Stockade he said: "This is critical ground—taking it means survival.
translations.idiomatic: Bin led three thousand infantry and cavalry on a punitive expedition. In the heat of summer he forced the march day and night. Reaching Huaiyuan Stockade he said, "This is the key ground. Seize it and we live.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「奈何背龍江邪？」

translations.literal: Someone said: "How can we turn our backs to Long River?
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "How can we turn our backs to the Long River?

sentences.zh: 笑曰：「是所以生也。」

translations.literal: He laughed and said: "That is precisely why we shall live.
translations.idiomatic: He laughed and said, "That is precisely why we shall live.

sentences.zh: 因示弱驕之，蠻果大至，斌選將迎敵，戒以遇之則走，誘至平阪，列八陣以待之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he feigned weakness to make them arrogant; the Man indeed came in great force. Bin selected generals to meet the enemy, instructing them that upon encounter they should flee, luring them to level ground, where he deployed the Eight Formations to await them.
translations.idiomatic: He then deliberately showed weakness to goad them into overconfidence, and the tribesmen came in full force as expected. Bin chose officers to meet them and ordered them to retreat on contact, drawing the enemy onto open ground where he had drawn up the Eight Formations in waiting.

sentences.zh: 張疑兵左右山上，蠻登嶺望見，始大驚。

translations.literal: He posted dummy troops on the hills to left and right; the Man climbed the ridge and saw them, and at last were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: He had placed decoy troops on the hills to either flank. When the tribesmen climbed a ridge and saw them, they were at last thrown into great alarm.

sentences.zh: 斌分騎翼其旁，自被甲步出，為眾士先，殊死戰。

translations.literal: Bin divided cavalry to flank them on the sides; he himself donned armor and marched out on foot, taking the lead among all the soldiers, fighting desperately.
translations.idiomatic: Bin split his cavalry to attack from the flanks. He personally donned armor and marched out on foot at the head of the men, fighting with utter desperation.

sentences.zh: 蠻大敗，世念率酋黨四千八百內附。

translations.literal: The Man suffered a great defeat; Shinan led four thousand eight hundred chieftains and followers in submitting to the interior.
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen were routed. Shinan led four thousand eight hundred chieftains and followers in surrendering to the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 遂以榮州團練使知宜州，遷西上閣門使、知邕州，以老請還，除高陽關副總管，曆永興軍路。

translations.literal: He was then made Militia Commissioner of Rongzhou and given charge of Yizhou; promoted to Western Upper Gate Commissioner and given charge of Yongzhou; on account of age he requested to return and was appointed Deputy Overall Commander of Gaoyang Pass, serving along the Yongxing Army circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed militia commissioner of Rong while administering Yizhou, then promoted to Western Upper Gate Commissioner and put in charge of Yong. When age prompted him to ask for recall, he was made deputy overall commander at Gaoyang Pass and served successively along the Yongxing circuit.

sentences.zh: 召拜龍、神衛四廂都指揮，至步軍都虞候，卒，年八十。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Commander of the Four Wings of the Dragon and Divine Guard Armies, reaching Vice Commander of the Infantry Armies; he died at age eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court and appointed commander of the four wings of the Dragon and Divine Guard armies, rising finally to vice commander of the infantry. He died at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 贈寧州防禦使。

translations.literal: Posthumously gifted the title of Defense Commissioner of Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as defense commissioner of Ning.

sentences.zh: 斌老於為將，以恩信得邊人心，嶺南珍貨，一無所蓄。

translations.literal: Bin was old in serving as general; through kindness and faithfulness he won the hearts of men on the frontier; for rare treasures of Lingnan he amassed nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was a veteran commander who won over the frontier through kindness and trustworthiness. Of Lingnan's rare luxuries he kept nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 邊吏欲希功造事，皆憚不敢發；

translations.literal: Border officials who wished to seek merit by fabricating incidents all feared him and did not dare to stir up trouble;
translations.idiomatic: Border officials eager to manufacture incidents for merit all feared him and dared not provoke trouble;

sentences.zh: 或巧為諜報啟釁，亦必折其奸謀。

translations.literal: if some craftily made spy reports to start conflict, he would inevitably frustrate their treacherous schemes.
translations.idiomatic: and if any craftily fabricated intelligence to provoke conflict, he unfailingly crushed their designs.

sentences.zh: 故所至無事，士大夫稱之。

translations.literal: Therefore wherever he went there was no trouble, and scholar-officials praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served, the border stayed quiet, and scholars and officials praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 子 詵

translations.literal: Son: Shen
translations.idiomatic: Son: Shen

sentences.zh: 子詵，以蔭為河北副將，累官至右武大夫、威州刺史、知雄州。

translations.literal: His son Shen, through yin privilege became deputy general of Hebei; by successive promotions he reached Right Martial Grand Master, Prefect of Weizhou, and given charge of Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shen entered service through hereditary privilege as a deputy general in Hebei and rose through successive posts to Right Martial Grand Master, prefect of Wei, and military administrator of Xiong.

sentences.zh: 上制勝強遠弓式，能破堅于三百步外，邊人號為「鳳凰弓。」

translations.literal: The court devised the Victory-at-Distance bow pattern, able to pierce armor at over three hundred paces; border people called it the "Phoenix Bow.
translations.idiomatic: The court designed a new long-range Victory Bow pattern capable of piercing armor at three hundred paces and beyond. Border folk called it the "Phoenix Bow.

sentences.zh: 進相州觀察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 在雄十年，頗能偵敵。

translations.literal: While at Xiong for ten years, he was quite capable at scouting the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: During ten years at Xiong he proved skilled at enemy reconnaissance.

sentences.zh: 童貫攻燕，召詵計事，悅之。

translations.literal: When Tong Guan attacked Yan, he summoned Shen to consult on affairs and was pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong Guan launched the Yan campaign, he summoned Shen for counsel and was much taken with him.

sentences.zh: 分麾下兵俾以副統制，從种師道軍于白溝，旬有二日而退。

translations.literal: He assigned troops from under his command to Shen as deputy overall commander; he followed Zhong Shidao's army at Baigou and withdrew after twelve days.
translations.idiomatic: He detached part of his force to serve under Shen as deputy overall commander, who followed Zhong Shidao's army to Baigou and withdrew after twelve days.

sentences.zh: 追兵至，北風，大雨雹，師不能視。

translations.literal: Pursuing troops arrived; a north wind blew and heavy hail fell; the army could not see.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuers closed in. A north wind rose and heavy hail fell until the army could hardly see.

sentences.zh: 契丹以背盟譙責，薄暮，始得還。

translations.literal: The Khitan upbraided them for breaking the alliance; at dusk they at last got back.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan rebuked them for breach of alliance. Only at dusk did they manage to get back.

sentences.zh: 於是貫以契丹尚盛未可圖，劾詵覘候不實，貶濠州團練副使，筠州安置。

translations.literal: Thereupon Tong Guan, holding that the Khitan were still strong and could not be contemplated, impeached Shen for false reconnaissance, demoting him to Deputy Militia Commissioner of Haozhou, with resettlement at Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Guan, judging the Khitan still too strong to challenge, impeached Shen for inaccurate intelligence. He was demoted to deputy militia commissioner of Hao and ordered to reside at Yun.

sentences.zh: 詵始興取燕之謀，見事勢浸異，則又以為不宜取，故平燕肆赦，獨不得還。

translations.literal: Shen had first advocated the plan to take Yan; seeing the situation gradually change, he then also held that it ought not be taken; therefore when Yan was pacified and amnesty was proclaimed, he alone was not allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: Shen had been among the first to urge the conquest of Yan, but as events shifted he came to argue against it. When the Yan campaign ended in a general amnesty, he alone was excluded from recall.

sentences.zh: 後復官，卒。

translations.literal: Later his office was restored; he died.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was later restored, and he died.

sentences.zh: 劉仲武

translations.literal: Liu Zhongwu
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhongwu

sentences.zh: 劉仲武，字子文，秦州成紀人。

translations.literal: Liu Zhongwu, style name Ziwen, was a man of Chengji in Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhongwu, courtesy name Ziwen, was a native of Chengji in Qin.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，試射殿庭異等，補官。

translations.literal: In the Xining era, he tested archery in the palace hall at exceptional grade and received appointment.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining reign he tested archery in the palace court at the highest grade and received an official appointment.

sentences.zh: 數從軍，累轉禮賓使，為涇原將。

translations.literal: He went on campaign several times, was promoted successively to Ritual Reception Commissioner, and served as a general of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After several campaigns he rose to Ritual Reception Commissioner and served as a general on the Jingyuan front.

sentences.zh: 夏人謀犯天聖砦，渭帥檄諸將會兵，約曰：「過某日賊不至，即去。」

translations.literal: The Xi Xia planned to attack Tiansheng Stockade; the Wei commander issued orders to the generals to muster troops, stipulating: "If after such-and-such day the bandits do not come, then depart.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut planned to attack Tiansheng Stockade, the commander of Wei ordered the generals to assemble and stipulated, "If the enemy fails to appear by the appointed day, withdraw.

sentences.zh: 仲武諜得的期，乞緩分屯。

translations.literal: Zhongwu's spies learned the expected date and he requested delaying the dispersed encampments.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu's scouts learned the enemy's intended date of attack and asked that the dispersed encampments be held longer.

sentences.zh: 帥不樂，但留一將及仲武軍，如期而敵至，力戰卻之。

translations.literal: The commander was displeased, but kept only one general along with Zhongwu's army; on the appointed day the enemy arrived and they fought fiercely and repulsed them.
translations.idiomatic: The commander was displeased but left only one general with Zhongwu's force. On the appointed day the enemy came, and after hard fighting they were driven back.

sentences.zh: 遷皇城使、熙河都監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Imperial City Commissioner and Overall Supervisor of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Imperial City Commissioner and overall supervisor of the Xihe circuit.

sentences.zh: 復湟州，進東上閣門使、知河州。

translations.literal: He recovered Huangzhou; promoted to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner and given charge of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered Huang and was promoted to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner with charge of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃趙懷德、狼阿章眾數萬叛命，仲武相持數日，潛遣二將領千騎扣其營，戒曰：「彼出，勿與戰，亟還，伏兵道左。」

translations.literal: The Tibetans Zhao Huaide and Lang'azhang with tens of thousands rebelled; Zhongwu confronted them for several days, secretly sent two generals leading a thousand cavalry to strike their camp, instructing: "If they come out, do not fight; return quickly; ambush troops on the left of the road.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan leaders Zhao Huaide and Lang'azhang rebelled with a force of tens of thousands. After confronting them for several days, Zhongwu secretly sent two generals with a thousand horsemen to raid their camp, with orders: "If they sally out, do not engage—withdraw at once while ambush troops lie in wait on the left of the road.

sentences.zh: 二將還，羌果追之，遇伏大敗，斬首三千級，復西寧州。

translations.literal: The two generals returned; the Qiang indeed pursued them, encountered the ambush and were greatly defeated; three thousand heads were cut off; Xining prefecture was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The two generals fell back as ordered; the Qiang pursued and ran into the ambush, suffering a crushing defeat. Three thousand heads were taken and Xining was recovered.

sentences.zh: 未幾，懷德、阿章降。

translations.literal: Before long, Huaide and Azhang surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Huaide and Azhang submitted.

sentences.zh: 累進客省使、榮州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was promoted successively to Guest Reception Commissioner and Defense Commissioner of Rongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Guest Reception Commissioner and defense commissioner of Rong.

sentences.zh: 副高永年西征。

translations.literal: He served as deputy to Gao Yongnian on the western expedition.
translations.idiomatic: He served as deputy to Gao Yongnian on the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 仲武欲持重固壘，永年易賊輕戰，遂大敗。

translations.literal: Zhongwu wished to hold fast and fortify camp; Yongnian underestimated the enemy and fought lightly, and so suffered great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu urged a cautious defense behind fortified camps, but Yongnian treated the enemy lightly and rushed into battle, leading to catastrophic defeat.

sentences.zh: 仲武引咎自劾，坐流嶺南。

translations.literal: Zhongwu took blame and impeached himself; sentenced to exile in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu accepted blame and submitted a self-impeachment. He was sentenced to exile in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 命未下，與夏人戰，傷足。

translations.literal: Before the order was issued, he fought with the Xi Xia and was wounded in the foot.
translations.idiomatic: Before the sentence could be issued, he fought the Tangut again and was wounded in the foot.

sentences.zh: 朝廷閔之，貸其罰，以為西寧都護。

translations.literal: The court took pity on him, remitted his punishment, and made him Protector-General of Xining.
translations.idiomatic: The court took pity on him, remitted his punishment, and appointed him protector-general of Xining.

sentences.zh: 童貫招誘羌王子臧征僕哥，收積石軍，邀仲武計事。

translations.literal: Tong Guan enticed the Qiang prince Zangzheng Puge, recovered Jishi Army, and invited Zhongwu to consult on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Guan worked to win over the Qiang prince Zangzheng Puge, recovered Jishi Army, and summoned Zhongwu for counsel.

sentences.zh: 仲武曰：「王師入，羌必降；

translations.literal: Zhongwu said: "When the imperial army enters, the Qiang will surely surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu said, "When the imperial army enters, the Qiang will surely submit;

sentences.zh: 或退伏巢穴，可乘其便。

translations.literal: or if they withdraw and hide in their lairs, their convenience may be seized.
translations.idiomatic: or if they retreat into their mountain strongholds, we can exploit the opening.

sentences.zh: 但河橋功力大，非倉卒可成，緩急要預辦耳。

translations.literal: But the river bridge requires great labor and cannot be completed in haste; for emergency it must be prepared in advance.
translations.idiomatic: But building the river bridge is a major undertaking and cannot be finished overnight—it must be prepared well in advance for whatever urgency arises.

sentences.zh: 若稟命待報，慮失事機。」

translations.literal: If one reports up and waits for reply, I fear the opportunity will be lost.
translations.idiomatic: If we wait for orders from above, I fear we will miss the moment.

sentences.zh: 貫許以便宜。

translations.literal: Guan granted him discretionary authority.
translations.idiomatic: Guan authorized him to act at his own discretion.

sentences.zh: 僕哥果約降，而索一子為質。

translations.literal: Puge indeed agreed to surrender, but demanded one son as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Puge did agree to surrender, but demanded that one of Zhongwu's sons be sent as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 仲武即遣子錫往，河橋亦成。

translations.literal: Zhongwu immediately sent his son Xi; the river bridge was also completed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu at once sent his son Xi, and the river bridge was completed as well.

sentences.zh: 仲武帥師渡河，挈與歸。

translations.literal: Zhongwu led the army across the river and brought him back with them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu led his army across the river and brought Puge back with him.

sentences.zh: 貫掩其功，仲武亦不自言。

translations.literal: Guan concealed his merit; Zhongwu also did not speak of it himself.
translations.idiomatic: Guan suppressed credit for the achievement, and Zhongwu said nothing of it himself.

sentences.zh: 徽宗遣使持錢至邊，賜獲王者。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong sent envoys bearing money to the frontier to reward those who had captured kings.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong sent envoys with cash to the frontier to reward those who had taken enemy rulers.

sentences.zh: 訪得仲武，召對，帝勞之曰：「高永年以不用卿言失律，僕哥之降，河南綏定，卿力也。」

translations.literal: When they found Zhongwu and summoned him for audience, the Emperor commended him, saying: "Gao Yongnian violated discipline for not heeding your words; Puge's surrender and the pacification of Henan are your doing.
translations.idiomatic: When inquiry led them to Zhongwu, he was summoned for audience. The Emperor commended him, saying, "Gao Yongnian fell into disorder for failing to heed your counsel. Puge's surrender and the pacification of the region south of the river were your achievement.

sentences.zh: 問幾子，曰：「九人。」

translations.literal: He asked how many sons; he replied: "Nine.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked how many sons he had. He answered, "Nine.

sentences.zh: 悉命以官，錫閣門祗候。

translations.literal: All were ordered given offices; Xi received Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered all of them given official posts; Xi was appointed Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 仲武知西寧州，徙渭州，召為龍、神衛都指揮使，復出熙州、秦州，遷步軍副都指揮使。

translations.literal: Zhongwu administered Xining prefecture, was transferred to Weizhou, summoned as Commander of the Dragon and Divine Guard Armies, again sent out to Xizhou and Qinzhou, and promoted to Deputy Commander of the Infantry Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu served as prefect of Xining, was transferred to Wei, recalled as commander of the Dragon and Divine Guard armies, sent out again to Xi and Qin, and promoted to deputy commander of the infantry.

sentences.zh: 熙帥劉法死，又以熙、渭都統制攝之。

translations.literal: When the Xi commander Liu Fa died, he was again made acting Overall Commander of Xi and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xi commander Liu Fa died, he was again appointed acting overall commander of Xi and Wei.

sentences.zh: 曆拜徐州觀察使、保靜軍承宣使、瀘川軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was successively appointed Governor of Xuzhou, Commissioner of the Baojing Army, and Military Commissioner of the Luchuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments as governor of Xu, commissioner of the Baojing Army, and military commissioner of the Luchuan circuit.

sentences.zh: 以老，提舉明道宮，再起為熙州。

translations.literal: On account of age he was made Superintendent of Mingdao Palace; later he was again appointed to Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When age told against him, he was made superintendent of Mingdao Palace, but was later recalled to serve at Xi.

sentences.zh: 卒於官，年七三。

translations.literal: He died in office at age seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 贈檢校少保，諡曰威肅。

translations.literal: Posthumously gifted the title of Investigating and Pacifying Junior Guardian; posthumous title Wei Su.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Investigating and Pacifying Junior Guardian and given the posthumous title Wei Su, "Formidable and Stern."

sentences.zh: 子錡，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Qi has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qi is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 曲珍，字君玉，隴幹人，世為著姓。

translations.literal: Qu Zhen, style name Junyu, was a man of Longgan; his family for generations was a prominent clan.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Zhen, courtesy name Junyu, was a native of Longgan from a family that had been prominent for generations.

sentences.zh: 寶元、康定間，夏人數入寇，珍諸父糾集族党禦之，敵不敢犯。

translations.literal: Between the Baoyuan and Kangding reigns, the Xi Xia repeatedly invaded; Zhen's uncles gathered clan members to resist them, and the enemy did not dare to violate them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoyuan and Kangding reigns, when the Tangut repeatedly raided the frontier, Zhen's uncles rallied the clan to resist, and the enemy did not dare approach.

sentences.zh: 於是曲氏以材武長雄邊關。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Qu clan, through talent and martial prowess, grew dominant on the border passes.
translations.idiomatic: From this the Qu clan came to dominate the frontier through martial prowess.

sentences.zh: 珍好馳馬試劍，嘗與叔父出塞游獵，猝遇夏人，陷其圍中。

translations.literal: Zhen loved galloping horses and testing swords; once he went beyond the passes with his uncle to hunt, suddenly encountered the Xi Xia, and fell into their encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen loved horsemanship and swordplay. Once, hunting beyond the frontier with his uncle, he suddenly ran into Tangut troops and was trapped in their encirclement.

sentences.zh: 馳擊大呼，眾披靡，得出，顧叔不至，復持短兵還決鬥，遂俱脫。

translations.literal: He charged shouting; the masses scattered and he got out; seeing his uncle had not arrived, he again took short weapons and returned to fight decisively, and so both escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He charged in shouting, scattering the enemy and breaking free. Finding his uncle had not emerged, he turned back with a short weapon to fight his way through again, and both escaped.

sentences.zh: 秦鳳都鈐轄劉溫潤奇其材，一日，出寶劍令曰：「能射一錢于百步外者，與之。」

translations.literal: Qin-Feng Overall Commander Liu Wenrun marveled at his talent; one day he produced a treasured sword and ordered: "Whoever can shoot through a coin at over a hundred paces shall have it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenrun, overall commander of Qin and Feng, admired his talent. One day he brought out a fine sword and announced, "Whoever can pierce a coin at a hundred paces shall have it.

sentences.zh: 諸少年百發不能中，珍後至，一矢破之。

translations.literal: The young men shot a hundred times and could not hit it; Zhen arrived later and with one arrow pierced it.
translations.idiomatic: The young men shot a hundred times without hitting the mark. Zhen arrived last and split the coin with a single arrow.

sentences.zh: 從溫潤城古渭，與羌戰，先登陷陳。

translations.literal: He followed Wenrun in fortifying Guwei, fought with the Qiang, and was first to ascend and break the enemy line.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Wenrun in building the fort at Guwei, fought the Qiang, and was first over the wall to break the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 為綏德城監押，提孤軍拒寇，斬其大酋，加閣門祗候。

translations.literal: He served as garrison commander of Suide city, led an isolated army to resist the invaders, beheaded their great chieftain, and was promoted to Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: As garrison commander of Suide, he led a lone detachment against the raiders, killed their chief chieftain, and was promoted to Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 有功洮西，遷內殿崇班。

translations.literal: Having merit on the west of the Tao, he was transferred to Inner Hall Honored Rank.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements west of the Tao River he was promoted to Inner Hall Honored Rank.

sentences.zh: 郭逵、趙禼南征，為第一將。

translations.literal: When Guo Kui and Zhao Jie marched south, he served as First General.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Kui and Zhao Jie led the southern campaign, he served as first general.

sentences.zh: 進自右江，撫接廣源三州十二縣，降偽守已下百六十人，老稚三萬六千口。

translations.literal: Advancing from the Right River, he pacified and received the three prefectures and twelve counties of Guangyuan, receiving the surrender of one hundred sixty persons from false prefects downward, and old and young totaling thirty-six thousand mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing from the Right River, he pacified the three prefectures and twelve counties of Guangyuan, accepting the surrender of one hundred sixty officials down to the level of prefect, along with thirty-six thousand men, women, and children.

sentences.zh: 是行也，功最諸將，遷西染院使。

translations.literal: On this expedition his merit ranked highest among the generals; he was transferred to Commissioner of the Western Dyeing Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: On this campaign his achievements ranked first among the generals, and he was promoted to Commissioner of the Western Dyeing Bureau.

sentences.zh: 得疾，輿還京師，神宗遣使臨問，少間，令入對。

translations.literal: He fell ill and was carried back to the capital; Emperor Shenzong sent envoys to inquire in person; shortly afterward he was ordered to enter for audience.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and was carried back to the capital. Emperor Shenzong sent envoys to inquire after him, and shortly afterward summoned him for audience.

sentences.zh: 珍念二帥不和睦，上問必及之，言之必形曲直，將何以對，乃以余疾未平為解。

translations.literal: Zhen reflected that the two commanders were not harmonious; if the Emperor asked he would surely touch on it, and speaking would necessarily reveal right and wrong—how could he answer? He therefore pleaded that his illness had not yet subsided.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen knew the two commanders were at odds. The Emperor was sure to ask about it, and any answer would expose who was right and who was wrong—so he pleaded that his illness had not yet fully passed.

sentences.zh: 帝復使獎勞，賜之弓劍、鞍勒，命有司蠲其鄉徭斌，擢鄜延鈐轄，進副總管。

translations.literal: The Emperor again sent envoys to reward and comfort him, bestowing bow, sword, and saddle trappings, ordering the relevant offices to exempt his home district corvee duties, promoting him to Overall Commander of Yan-Yan, and advancing him to Deputy Overall Commander.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again sent envoys with rewards, granting him bow, sword, and saddle trappings, ordering his home district corvee duties remitted, promoting him to overall commander of Yan-Yan, and advancing him to deputy overall commander.

sentences.zh: 從种諤攻金湯、永平川，斬二千級。

translations.literal: He followed Chong E in attacking Jintang and Yongpingchuan, cutting off two thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Chong E in the assault on Jintang and Yongpingchuan, taking two thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 累遷客省使，拜懷州防禦使、龍神衛四廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: He was promoted successively to Guest Reception Commissioner and appointed Defense Commissioner of Huaizhou and Commander of the Four Wings of the Dragon and Divine Guard Armies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Guest Reception Commissioner and was appointed defense commissioner of Huai and commander of the four wings of the Dragon and Divine Guard armies.

sentences.zh: 徐禧城永樂，珍以兵從。

translations.literal: When Xu Xi fortified Yongle, Zhen followed with troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Xi built the fortress at Yongle, Zhen accompanied him with troops.

sentences.zh: 版築方興，羌數十騎濟無定河覘役，珍將追殺之，禧不許。

translations.literal: While rampart building was just underway, several dozen Qiang horsemen crossed the Wuding River to spy on the labor; Zhen was about to pursue and kill them, but Xi would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: While construction was still underway, several dozen Qiang horsemen crossed the Wuding River to reconnoiter the work. Zhen wanted to pursue and kill them, but Xi refused.

sentences.zh: 諜言夏人聚兵甚急，珍請禧還米脂而自居守。

translations.literal: Spies reported that the Xi Xia were gathering troops with great urgency; Zhen asked Xi to return to Mizhi while he himself remained to hold the fort.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligence reported that the Tangut were massing troops with great urgency. Zhen urged Xi to withdraw to Mizhi while he himself held the fort.

sentences.zh: 明日果至，禧復來，珍曰：「敵兵眾甚，公宜退處內柵，檄諸將促戰。」

translations.literal: The next day they indeed arrived; Xi came back again; Zhen said: "The enemy troops are very numerous; you should withdraw to the inner palisade and issue orders to the generals to press the battle.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy came the next day as predicted, and Xi returned. Zhen said, "The enemy force is very large. You should withdraw to the inner palisade and order the generals to engage.

sentences.zh: 禧笑曰：「曲侯老將，何怯邪？」

translations.literal: Xi laughed and said: "Commander Qu, old general—why so timid?
translations.idiomatic: Xi laughed and said, "Commander Qu, you old veteran—why so timid?

sentences.zh: 夏兵且濟，珍欲乘其未集擊之，又不許。

translations.literal: The Xi Xia troops were about to cross the river; Zhen wished to strike them before they had assembled, but again was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: As the Tangut were about to cross the river, Zhen wanted to attack before they could assemble, but again Xi refused.

sentences.zh: 及攻城急，又勸禧曰：「城中井深泉嗇，士卒渴甚，恐不能支。

translations.literal: When the siege pressed hard, he again urged Xi, saying: "The wells in the city are deep and water scarce; the soldiers are very thirsty—I fear they cannot hold out.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege intensified, he again urged Xi, "The wells are deep and water scarce; the men are parched with thirst. I fear we cannot hold out.

sentences.zh: 宜乘兵氣未衰，潰圍而出，使人自求生。」

translations.literal: It would be well to take advantage while fighting spirit has not yet waned, break out of encirclement, and let each man seek his own survival.
translations.idiomatic: We should break out while morale still holds and let the men save themselves.

sentences.zh: 禧曰：「此城據要地，奈何棄之？

translations.literal: Xi said: "This city occupies critical ground—how can we abandon it?
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "This fortress holds a vital position—how can we abandon it?

sentences.zh: 且為將而奔，眾心搖矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover, for a general to flee—the hearts of the masses will waver.
translations.idiomatic: And if the commander runs, the men's hearts will fail.

sentences.zh: 珍曰：「非敢自愛，但敕使、謀臣同沒於此，懼辱國耳。」

translations.literal: Zhen said: "I do not dare spare myself, but the imperial envoy and planning ministers would perish here together—I fear disgracing the state.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, "It is not that I value my own life, but that the imperial envoy and staff advisers would perish here together—I fear the disgrace to the state.

sentences.zh: 數日城陷，珍縋而免，子弟死者六人。

translations.literal: Within several days the city fell; Zhen escaped by rope; six of his sons and younger brothers died.
translations.idiomatic: Within days the city fell. Zhen lowered himself by rope and escaped, but six of his sons and younger brothers were killed.

sentences.zh: 亦坐貶皇城使。

translations.literal: He was also demoted to Imperial City Commissioner on account of it.
translations.idiomatic: He was also demoted to Imperial City Commissioner for his part in the disaster.

sentences.zh: 帝察其無罪，諭使自安養，以圖後效。

translations.literal: The Emperor perceived he was without guilt and instructed him to rest and recuperate, looking to future merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor saw that he was not at fault and told him to rest and recover, with an eye to future service.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，為環慶副總管。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanyou era, he served as Deputy Overall Commander of Huan-Qing.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yuanyou reign he served as deputy overall commander of Huan-Qing.

sentences.zh: 夏人寇涇原，號四十萬，珍搗虛馳三百里，破之曲律山，俘斬千八百人，解其圍。

translations.literal: The Xi Xia raided Jingyuan, claiming four hundred thousand; Zhen struck their rear and raced three hundred li, defeating them at Qulü Mountain, capturing and beheading one thousand eight hundred men, and relieving the siege.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut raided Jingyuan with a force they claimed numbered four hundred thousand, Zhen struck at their rear, riding three hundred li in a forced march to defeat them at Qulü Mountain, killing or capturing eighteen hundred men and lifting the siege.

sentences.zh: 進東上閤門使、忠州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner and Defense Commissioner of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner and defense commissioner of Zhong.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: He died at age fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 珍善撫士卒，得其死力。

translations.literal: Zhen was skilled at comforting soldiers and obtained their strength unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen knew how to treat his soldiers well and won their loyalty unto death.

sentences.zh: 雖不知書，而忠樸好義，本於天性。

translations.literal: Although he did not know books, he was loyal, plain, and fond of righteousness—rooted in his inborn nature.
translations.idiomatic: Though he could not read, he was loyal, plainspoken, and devoted to duty by nature.

sentences.zh: 劉闃，字靜叔，青州北海人。

translations.literal: Liu Qu, style name Jing Shu, was a native of Beihai in Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qu, courtesy name Jing Shu, was a native of Beihai in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以拳力為軍校，從延州軍出塞遇敵，矢貫左耳，戰不顧，眾服其勇。

translations.literal: For his wrestling strength he became a military officer; with the Yanzhou army he went beyond the frontier and met the enemy. An arrow pierced his left ear, yet he did not cease fighting—the troops admired his courage.
translations.idiomatic: Enlisted as a military officer for his wrestling prowess, he marched beyond the frontier with the Yanzhou army and met the enemy. An arrow pierced his left ear, but he fought on without flinching, and the men admired his courage.

sentences.zh: 從文彥博討貝州，次城下，攀壘欲登，賊以曲戟鉤其甲，闃裂之而墜。

translations.literal: He followed Wen Yanbo in suppressing Beizhou, halted beneath the city walls, climbed the ramparts intending to ascend; the rebels hooked his armor with a curved halberd—Qu tore it free and fell.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Wen Yanbo in the campaign against Beizhou. Halting beneath the walls, he climbed the ramparts to scale them, but the rebels caught his armor with a curved halberd. Qu ripped free and fell.

sentences.zh: 議者欲穿地道入，闃曰：「穴地積土，賊且知之。

translations.literal: Those in council wished to tunnel underground to enter. Qu said: "If you dig earth and pile up soil, the rebels will soon know.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed digging a tunnel to enter the city. Qu said, "Digging earth and piling it up—the rebels will soon find out.

sentences.zh: 城瀕河，若晝囊土而夜投諸河，宜無知者。」

translations.literal: The city borders a river—if by day you bag the soil and by night throw it into the river, presumably none would know."
translations.idiomatic: The city stands on the river. If we bag the soil by day and dump it in the river at night, no one should notice."

sentences.zh: 彥博以為然。

translations.literal: Yanbo thought this correct.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo agreed.

sentences.zh: 穴成，闃持短兵先入，眾始從，遂登陴，引繩而上，遲明，師畢入。

translations.literal: When the tunnel was complete, Qu took a short weapon and entered first; the troops then followed, ascended the battlements, drew ropes and went up—by late dawn the army had fully entered.
translations.idiomatic: When the tunnel was ready, Qu took a short weapon and went in first. The men then followed, reached the battlements, and hauled themselves up by rope. By late dawn the whole force was inside.

sentences.zh: 貝州平，功第一，擢虎翼指揮使。

translations.literal: Beizhou was pacified; his merit ranked first; he was promoted to Tiger Wings Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Beizhou was pacified, his merit ranked first and he was promoted to commandant of the Tiger Wings Guard.

sentences.zh: 累遷宣武神衛都指揮使、昭州刺史、辰州團練使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Xuanwu Spirit Guard Commander-in-Chief, Prefect of Zhao, and Militia Commissioner of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to commander-in-chief of the Xuanwu Spirit Guard, prefect of Zhao, and militia commissioner of Chen.

sentences.zh: 韓絳宣撫陝西，詔闃自河東為犄角。

translations.literal: When Han Jiang was pacification commissioner for Shaanxi, an edict ordered Qu to advance from Hedong in a pincer movement.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Jiang was appointed pacification commissioner for Shaanxi, an edict ordered Qu to move out from Hedong as a pincer force.

sentences.zh: 至鐵冶溝，夏人大集。

translations.literal: When they reached Tieye Gorge, the Tangut assembled in great force.
translations.idiomatic: At Tieye Gorge the Tangut gathered in overwhelming numbers.

sentences.zh: 眾懼，闃自殿后，率銳驍搏戰，飛矢蔽體不為卻，敵解去。

translations.literal: The troops were afraid; Qu personally brought up the rear, leading elite cavalry in fierce fighting—flying arrows covered his body yet he did not retreat; the enemy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The men were terrified. Qu himself covered the retreat, leading crack cavalry in a desperate fight. Arrows flew around him thick as a curtain, yet he did not give ground, and the enemy broke off.

sentences.zh: 為冀州駐泊總管。

translations.literal: He served as overall commander of the Jizhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He served as overall commander of the Jizhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 河水漲，堤防墊急，闃請郡守開青楊道口以殺水怒，莫敢任其責。

translations.literal: The river rose and the dikes were urgently threatened; Qu asked the prefect to open Qingyang Estuary to reduce the water's fury, but none dared assume responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: When the river swelled and the dikes were in imminent danger, Qu asked the prefect to open the Qingyang Estuary to bleed off the flood, but no one dared take responsibility.

sentences.zh: 闃躬往浚決，水退，冀人賴之。

translations.literal: Qu went personally to dredge and cut the channel; the water receded, and the people of Ji depended on him.
translations.idiomatic: Qu went in person to dredge and cut the channel. The water fell, and the people of Ji owed him their safety.

sentences.zh: 以左金吾大將軍致仕。

translations.literal: He retired as Left Gold Crow Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He retired with the rank of Left Gold Crow Grand General.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 郭成，字信之，德順中安堡人也。

translations.literal: Guo Cheng, style name Xin Zhi, was a man of Zhong'an Fort in Deshun.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Cheng, courtesy name Xin Zhi, was from Zhong'an Fort in Deshun.

sentences.zh: 從軍，得供奉官。

translations.literal: He joined the army and obtained the post of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He entered military service and was appointed a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 王師趨靈武，成將涇原兵擊破夏人於漫𠼪隘。

translations.literal: When the imperial army pressed toward Lingwu, Cheng led Jingyuan troops and defeated the Tangut at Mandeng Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army marched on Lingwu, Cheng led Jingyuan troops and routed the Tangut at Mandeng Pass.

sentences.zh: 至城下，有羌乘白馬馳突陣前，大將劉昌祚曰：「誰能取此者？」

translations.literal: Upon reaching beneath the walls, a Qiang on a white horse charged toward the front of the formation. Great general Liu Changzuo said: "Who can take this man?"
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the foot of the walls, a Qiang on a white horse charged straight at the front of the line. General Liu Changzuo cried, "Who can bring down that man?"

sentences.zh: 成躍馬梟其首以獻，進秩四等。

translations.literal: Cheng leaped on his horse, beheaded him and presented the head; his rank was raised four grades.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng spurred his horse forward, struck off the man's head, and presented it. His rank was raised four grades.

sentences.zh: 朝廷築平夏城，置將戍之，又環以五砦。

translations.literal: The court built Pingxia City, stationed a general to garrison it, and ringed it with five fortified camps.
translations.idiomatic: The court built Pingxia City, posted a general to hold it, and surrounded it with five fortified camps.

sentences.zh: 渭帥章楶問可守者于諸將，皆曰：「非郭成不可。」

translations.literal: Wei military commissioner Zhang Shu asked the generals who could hold it; all said: "None but Guo Cheng will do."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shu, military commissioner of Wei, asked his generals who could hold the city. All answered, "Only Guo Cheng will do."

sentences.zh: 遂使往守。

translations.literal: They then sent him to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: So he was sent to defend it.

sentences.zh: 夏人恚失地，空國入爭，謀曰：「平夏視諸壘最大，郭成最知兵。」

translations.literal: The Tangut resented losing the territory and marshaled the whole state's forces to contest it. Their plan was: "Pingxia is the largest of all the fortresses, and Guo Cheng knows warfare best."
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut, furious at losing the ground, emptied the realm to reclaim it. Their plan ran: "Pingxia is the largest of all the forts, and Guo Cheng is the best soldier among them."

sentences.zh: 遂自沒煙峽連營百里，飛石激火，晝夜不息。

translations.literal: They then from Moyan Gorge linked camps for a hundred li, hurling stones and fire, ceaselessly day and night.
translations.idiomatic: From Moyan Gorge they strung camps along a hundred li, raining stones and fire without pause, day and night.

sentences.zh: 成與折可適議乘勝深入，以萬騎異道並進，遂俘阿埋、都逋二大酋。

translations.literal: Cheng and She Kesui discussed pressing the advantage deep; with ten thousand cavalry advancing on separate routes in parallel, they captured the two great chieftains Amo and Dubo.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng and She Kesui agreed to press the victory with a deep strike. Ten thousand horsemen advanced on separate routes at once and captured the two great chieftains, Amo and Dubo.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，進雄州防禦使、涇原鈐轄。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, he was promoted to Defense Commissioner of Xiong and Military Control Commissioner of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the victory arrived, he was promoted to defense commissioner of Xiong and military control commissioner of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 徽宗詔諸軍並力築綏戎、懷戎二堡，成獨當合流之役，暴露雪中，感疾卒。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong ordered all armies to jointly build the two forts of Suirong and Huairong. Cheng alone bore the task at the river confluence, exposed in the snow, contracted illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong ordered every army to help build the forts of Suirong and Huairong. Cheng alone shouldered the work at the river junction, standing exposed in the snow until illness took him.

sentences.zh: 帝悼之甚，賻以金帛，官其子婿。

translations.literal: The Emperor mourned him deeply, granted silks and gold in condolence, and gave offices to his sons and sons-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor grieved deeply, sent gold and silks as condolence gifts, and granted offices to his sons and sons-in-law.

sentences.zh: 成輕財好施，名震西鄙。

translations.literal: Cheng was light with wealth and generous in giving; his fame shook the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng cared little for money and gave freely; his name resounded across the western marches.

sentences.zh: 既沒，廉訪使者王孝謁白於朝，帝手書報曰：「郭成盡忠報國，有功於民，宜載祀典。」

translations.literal: After his death, Investigation Commissioner Wang Xiaoye reported to the court. The Emperor wrote in his own hand in reply: "Guo Cheng served the state loyally and rendered merit to the people—he should be entered in the sacrificial canon."
translations.idiomatic: After his death, investigation commissioner Wang Xiaoye reported to the court. The Emperor wrote back in his own hand: "Guo Cheng served the state faithfully and benefited the people. He should be entered in the official register of sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 榜其廟曰「仁勇」雲。

translations.literal: A plaque on his temple reads "Benevolent and Brave."
translations.idiomatic: His temple was given the plaque "Benevolent and Brave."

sentences.zh: 子浩，紹興中為西邊大將，至節度使。

translations.literal: His son Hao became a great general on the western frontier during the Shaoxing era, rising to military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hao became a leading general on the western frontier under the Shaoxing reign, rising to military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 賈岩，字民瞻，開封人。

translations.literal: Jia Yan, style name Min Zhan, was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yan, courtesy name Min Zhan, was a native of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 少時，善騎射，喟然歎曰：「大丈夫生世，要當自奮，揚名顯親可也。」

translations.literal: In youth he excelled at horsemanship and archery. He sighed and said: "A true man born into the world ought to strive on his own—to make a name and bring honor to his parents."
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he excelled at riding and archery. He sighed and said, "A man born into this world ought to strive for himself—to win fame and bring honor to his parents."

sentences.zh: 遂起家從戎。

translations.literal: He then rose from obscurity to join the army.
translations.idiomatic: And with that he left home to take up arms.

sentences.zh: 神宗選材武，以為內殿承制、慶州荔原堡都監。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong selected men of martial talent and appointed him Inner Hall Assimilated Text Commissioner and Overall Commander of Liyuan Fort in Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong picked him for his martial talent and made him inner-hall assimilated-text commissioner and overall commander of Liyuan Fort in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 林廣討瀘夷，辟將前鋒。

translations.literal: When Lin Guang suppressed the Lu Yi, he recruited Yan as vanguard general.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Guang campaigned against the Lu tribes, he recruited Yan as vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 又為河東將，敗西夏兵於明堂川。

translations.literal: He also served as Hedong general and defeated Western Xia troops at Mingtang River.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as a Hedong general and defeated Western Xia forces at Mingtang River.

sentences.zh: 累功轉莊宅副使。

translations.literal: Accumulating merit, he was transferred to Deputy Commissioner of the Manor Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated victories he was promoted to deputy commissioner of the Manor Bureau.

sentences.zh: 遷路監。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Route Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to route supervisor.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，夏兵數萬圍麟州神堂砦甚急，岩以數百騎往援，令其下曰：「國家無事時，不惜厚祿養汝輩，正以待一旦之用耳。

translations.literal: During the Shaosheng era, tens of thousands of Tangut troops urgently besieged the Shentang Fort of Lin Prefecture. Yan went with several hundred horsemen to relieve them and told his men: "When the state is at peace it does not stint generous salaries to keep you—precisely in waiting for your use in a single hour.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaosheng reign, tens of thousands of Tangut troops pressed the siege of Shentang Fort in Lin Prefecture. Yan rode to the rescue with a few hundred horsemen and told his men, "In peacetime the state pays you generous salaries for no other reason than to use you when the moment comes.

sentences.zh: 今力雖不敵，吾誓以死報！」

translations.literal: Today though our strength does not match theirs, I swear to repay with my death!"
translations.idiomatic: Today we are outmatched, but I swear to repay the state with my life!"

sentences.zh: 眾感厲，即循屈野河行，且五里，據北攔坡嶺上，一矢殪其酋，眾駭潰。

translations.literal: The troops were moved and inspired; they at once followed the Quye River. After about five li they took position on the north slope of Bollan Ridge. One arrow killed their chieftain; the masses were terrified and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The men were stirred to fury. They followed the Quye River some five li, then took position on the north slope of Bollan Ridge. One arrow killed the enemy chieftain, and the host broke in panic.

sentences.zh: 哲宗嘉歎，賜以袍帶。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhezong praised and sighed; he was granted robe and belt.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhezong praised him warmly and granted him an official robe and belt.

sentences.zh: 知皇城使、威州刺史，遷路鈐轄。

translations.literal: Imperial City Commissioner, Prefect of Wei; promoted to Route Military Control Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was made imperial city commissioner and prefect of Wei, then promoted to route military control commissioner.

sentences.zh: 岩在兵間二十年，在智略，能拊禦士卒，所鄉輒勝。

translations.literal: Yan spent twenty years in the army; in strategic insight he could comfort and command soldiers—wherever he advanced he prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: Yan spent twenty years in the field. He had a strategist's mind, knew how to hearten and command his troops, and wherever he led them they won.

sentences.zh: 時以良將入對，留擢龍、神衛四廂都指揮使，遷步軍都虞候、濠州團練使。

translations.literal: Because he was regarded as an excellent general he was summoned to audience; he was retained and promoted to Overall Commander of the Four Wings of the Dragon and Spirit Guard, transferred to infantry adjutant and Militia Commissioner of Hao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Recognized as an outstanding commander, he was summoned to court, kept in the capital, and promoted to overall commander of the four wings of the Dragon and Spirit Guard, then transferred to infantry adjutant and militia commissioner of Hao.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十二，贈雄州防禦使。

translations.literal: He died at age fifty-two; posthumously conferred Defense Commissioner of Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-two and was posthumously made defense commissioner of Xiong.

sentences.zh: 張整，字成伯，亳州贊阝陽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zheng, style name Cheng Bo, was a native of Zanyang in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zheng, courtesy name Cheng Bo, was a native of Qiaoyang in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 初隸皇城司禦龍籍，補供奉官，為利、文州都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Initially he was enrolled in the Imperial City Office Dragon Guard roster, appointed Palace Attendant, and served as Overall Inspector of Li and Wen prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He first served on the Dragon Guard roster of the Imperial City Office, was appointed palace attendant, and became overall inspector of Li and Wen prefectures.

sentences.zh: 邊夷歲鈔省地，吏習不與校，至反遺之物，留久乃去。

translations.literal: Border tribes each year raided to seize territory; officials had grown accustomed to not contesting it—even returning things the tribes left behind, staying long before departing.
translations.idiomatic: Border tribes raided each year to seize land, and local officials had grown used to yielding—not even disputing what the tribes left behind, which they would keep for a long while before going.

sentences.zh: 整惡其貪暴無已，密募死士，時其來，掩擊幾盡。

translations.literal: Zheng hated their endless greed and violence; he secretly recruited men willing to die, timed their coming, and ambushed them—nearly wiping them out.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng loathed their endless greed and violence. He secretly recruited daredevils, waited for their next raid, and ambushed them, nearly wiping them out.

sentences.zh: 有司劾生事，神宗壯之，不問。

translations.literal: The responsible offices impeached him for provoking trouble; Emperor Shenzong admired his spirit and did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities impeached him for stirring up trouble, but Emperor Shenzong admired his boldness and took no action.

sentences.zh: 調荊湖將領，拓溪蠻地，築九城，董兵鎮守。

translations.literal: Transferred as Jinghu general, he expanded Man tribal territory, built nine walled cities, and supervised troops to garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to command on the Jinghu front, he pushed into Man territory, built nine walled towns, and stationed troops to hold them.

sentences.zh: 又破蠻於大田，歲中三遷。

translations.literal: He again defeated the Man at Datian; within the year he was promoted three times.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the Man again at Datian and received three promotions within a single year.

sentences.zh: 犬吉狑萬眾乘舟屯托口，迫黔江城，時守兵才五百，人情大恐。

translations.literal: Qujilin led tens of thousands by boat to encamp at Tuokou, pressing on Qianjiang city. The garrison then had only five hundred men; public sentiment was greatly fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Qujilin led tens of thousands in boats to camp at Tuokou, threatening Qianjiang city. The garrison had only five hundred men, and panic spread through the town.

sentences.zh: 整伏其半於托口旁，戒曰：「須吾旦度金鬥崖，舉幟，則噪而前。」

translations.literal: Zheng hid half his force beside Tuokou and warned: "You must wait until I at dawn cross Jindou Cliff and raise the banner—then shout and advance."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng hid half his force near Tuokou and ordered, "Wait until I cross Jindou Cliff at dawn and raise the banner—then charge with a shout."

sentences.zh: 及旦，率其半，縛艨艟，建旗鼓，溯流急趨。

translations.literal: At dawn he led his half, lashed together warships, raised banners and drums, and rushed upstream.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he led the other half, lashed warships together, raised banners and drums, and raced upstream.

sentences.zh: 賊望見大笑。

translations.literal: The rebels saw them and laughed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy saw them and laughed.

sentences.zh: 幟舉伏發，前後合擊，人人殊死鬥，蠻騰踐投江中，殺獲不可計。

translations.literal: When the banner rose the hidden force struck; front and rear combined in attack—every man fought to the death. The Man leapt and trampled one another into the river; kills and captures were beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: When the banner went up the ambush sprang. Front and rear closed in, and every man fought as if for his life. The Man trampled one another into the river; the dead and captured were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 為廣西鈐轄，坐殺降徭，責監江州酒稅。

translations.literal: As Military Control Commissioner of Guangxi he was punished for killing surrendered Yao and was demoted to supervisor of Ji Prefecture wine taxes.
translations.idiomatic: As military control commissioner of Guangxi he was punished for slaughtering surrendered Yao and was demoted to supervising wine taxes at Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 復為涇原、真定、京東、環慶鈐轄。

translations.literal: He again served as Military Control Commissioner of Jingyuan, Zhending, Jingdong, and Huanqing.
translations.idiomatic: He later served again as military control commissioner of Jingyuan, Zhending, Jingdong, and Huanqing.

sentences.zh: 整蒞軍嚴明，哲宗嘗訪於輔臣，召之對，擢為龍神衛四廂都指揮使、管幹馬軍司。

translations.literal: Zheng was strict and clear in commanding the army. Emperor Zhezong once inquired of his chief ministers; summoned to audience, he was promoted to Overall Commander of the Four Wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard and Superintendent of the Horse Army Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng ran his command with stern discipline. Emperor Zhezong once asked his chief ministers about him, summoned him to court, and promoted him to overall commander of the four wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard and superintendent of the Horse Army Bureau.

sentences.zh: 卒，官至威州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; at death he held the office of Prefect of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the rank of prefect of Wei.

sentences.zh: 張蘊，字積之，開封將家子也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yun, style name Ji Zhi, was a son of a Kaifeng military family.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yun, courtesy name Ji Zhi, came from a military family in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 從軍為小校，隸劉昌祚。

translations.literal: He joined the army as a petty officer under Liu Changzuo.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the army as a junior officer under Liu Changzuo.

sentences.zh: 至靈州，遇敵中矢，拔鏃復戰，以功賜金帶。

translations.literal: At Lingzhou he met the enemy and was struck by an arrow; he pulled out the arrowhead and fought again; for his merit he was granted a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: At Lingzhou he met the enemy and took an arrow. He pulled out the head and fought on, and for his service was awarded a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 從征安南，次富良江，諸將猶豫未進，蘊褰裳先濟，眾隨之。

translations.literal: On the expedition against Annan he halted at the Fu River. The generals hesitated and did not advance; Yun lifted his robe and crossed first—the rest followed.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Annan he halted at the Fu River. The other generals hung back, but Yun hitched up his robe, waded across first, and the rest followed.

sentences.zh: 蠻遁走，使巫被發登崖為厭勝，蘊射之，應弦而斃，一軍歡噪。
