translations.literal: The Man fled; they sent a shaman with hair loose ascending a cliff to perform sorcery for victory. Yun shot him—he fell dead at the bowstring's release; the whole army shouted in joy.
translations.idiomatic: The Man fled. They sent a shaman with hair unbound up a cliff to work a spell against the army. Yun shot him, and he fell dead at the bowstring's snap. The whole force erupted in cheers.

sentences.zh: 曆京西、涇原將，知綏德、懷甯、順寧軍等六城，儲粟至三十萬斛。

translations.literal: He served successively as Jingxi and Jingyuan general, governing six walled cities including Suide, Huaining, and Shunning, and stored grain up to three hundred thousand hu.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as a Jingxi and Jingyuan commander, governing six walled posts including Suide, Huaining, and Shunning, and stockpiled grain to three hundred thousand hu.

sentences.zh: 將兵取宥州，破夏人于大吳神流堆。

translations.literal: He led troops to take You Prefecture and defeated the Tangut at Dawu Shenliu Mound.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops to seize You Prefecture and defeated the Tangut at Dawu Shenliu Mound.

sentences.zh: 宥州監軍引鐵騎數千趨松林堡，蘊諜知之，頓兵長城嶺以待，戒諸部曰：「賊遠來氣盛，少休必困，困而擊之，必捷。」

translations.literal: You Prefecture's military supervisor led several thousand iron cavalry toward Songlin Fort. Yun learned through spies; he halted his army at Great Wall Ridge to wait and warned the detachments: "The enemy has come far—their spirit is high. After brief rest they must grow weary; strike when weary and victory is certain."
translations.idiomatic: You Prefecture's military supervisor led several thousand iron cavalry toward Songlin Fort. Yun learned of it through spies, halted at Great Wall Ridge, and told his units, "The enemy has marched far and their spirits are high. Let them rest a little and they will tire—strike a tired foe and you are sure to win."

sentences.zh: 果以勝歸。

translations.literal: They indeed returned victorious.
translations.idiomatic: They returned victorious, as he had foretold.

sentences.zh: 夏人寇順寧，蘊置伏狹中，約聞呼則起，俘斬數百十人，獲馬、械甚眾。

translations.literal: When the Tangut raided Shunning, Yun set ambush in a narrow defile, agreeing that on hearing a shout they would rise; they captured and beheaded several hundred men and gained horses and weapons in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut raided Shunning, Yun hid men in a narrow pass with orders to rise at his shout. They killed or captured several hundred men and took horses and arms in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 累遷皇城使、榮州刺史、成州團練使、通州防禦使，開德、河陽馬步軍副總管。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Imperial City Commissioner, Prefect of Rong, Militia Commissioner of Cheng, Defense Commissioner of Tong, and Deputy Overall Commander of Kai and Heyang horse and foot armies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to imperial city commissioner, prefect of Rong, militia commissioner of Cheng, defense commissioner of Tong, and deputy overall commander of the Kai and Heyang horse and foot armies.

sentences.zh: 顯肅皇后母自鄭氏再適蘊，徽宗屢欲以恩進其官，輒力辭不敢受，人以為賢。

translations.literal: Empress Xiansu's mother, formerly of the Zheng clan, remarried Yun. Emperor Huizong repeatedly wished to advance his rank by grace; he always forcefully declined and dared not accept—people considered him worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiansu's mother, née Zheng, had remarried Yun. Emperor Huizong repeatedly tried to promote him as a favor, but Yun always refused firmly, and people judged him worthy for it.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十三，贈感德軍節度使，諡曰榮毅。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-three; posthumously conferred Military Commissioner of Gande; posthumous title Rong Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-three, was posthumously made military commissioner of Gande, and given the posthumous name Rongyi.

sentences.zh: 王恩，字澤之，開封人。

translations.literal: Wang En, style name Ze Zhi, was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang En, courtesy name Ze Zhi, was a native of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 以善射入羽林，神宗閱衛士，挽強中的，且偉其貌，補供備庫副使。

translations.literal: For skill in archery he entered the Feathered Forest Guard. When Emperor Shenzong reviewed the guards, he drew a strong bow and hit the target; moreover his appearance was imposing—he was appointed Deputy Commissioner of the Supply Reserve Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in archery, he joined the Feathered Forest Guard. When Emperor Shenzong reviewed the palace guards, En drew a heavy bow and hit the mark. Impressed by his bearing as well, the Emperor made him deputy commissioner of the Supply Reserve Bureau.

sentences.zh: 為河州巡檢，夏羌寇蘭州，恩搏戰城下，中兩矢，拔去復鬥，意氣彌厲。

translations.literal: As inspector of He Prefecture, when Tangut Qiang raided Lan Prefecture, En fought beneath the walls; struck by two arrows he pulled them out and fought again—his spirit grew fiercer still.
translations.idiomatic: As inspector of He Prefecture, he fought beneath the walls when Tangut Qiang raided Lan Prefecture. Hit by two arrows, he pulled them out and kept fighting, his fighting spirit only rising.

sentences.zh: 遷涇原將。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Jingyuan general.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general on the Jingyuan front.

sentences.zh: 嘗整軍出萬惠嶺。

translations.literal: He once led the army out through Wanhui Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Once, leading his troops out through Wanhui Ridge,

sentences.zh: 士饑欲食，恩倍道兼行，眾洶洶。

translations.literal: The men were hungry and wanted food; En pressed on by forced marches—the crowd grew clamorous.
translations.idiomatic: the men grew hungry and clamored for food. En forced the march at double speed, and the ranks grew restless.

sentences.zh: 已而遇敵數萬，引兵先入壁，井灶皆具，諸將始服。

translations.literal: Soon they met tens of thousands of the enemy; he led his troops first into the walled camp—wells and stoves were all prepared—the generals then submitted in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Then they ran into tens of thousands of the enemy. En led his men straight into a fortified camp where wells and cooking pits were already prepared. Only then did the other generals admit he had been right.

sentences.zh: 羌扣壁願見，恩單騎徑出，遙與語，一夕，羌引去。

translations.literal: The Qiang knocked on the fort seeking audience; En went out alone on horseback, spoke with them from afar; within one night the Qiang withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang beat on the fort walls asking to parley. En rode out alone, spoke with them from a distance, and by the next morning they had withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 哲宗召見，語左右曰：「先帝時宿衛人，皆傑異如此。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhezong summoned him to audience and said to those nearby: "The palace guard men of the late Emperor's time were all extraordinary like this."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhezong summoned him and said to those around him, "The palace guards of my father's day were full of men like this."

sentences.zh: 留為龍、神衛都指揮使，遷馬軍都虞候。

translations.literal: He was retained as Overall Commander of the Dragon and Spirit Guard, promoted to cavalry adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: En was kept at court as overall commander of the Dragon and Spirit Guard and promoted to cavalry adjutant.

sentences.zh: 契丹使來，詔陪射，使者問：「聞涇原有王騎將，得無是乎？」

translations.literal: When a Khitan envoy came, an edict ordered En to accompany him in archery. The envoy asked: "I hear in Jingyuan there is a Wang, a cavalry general—could this be he?"
translations.idiomatic: When a Khitan envoy arrived, an edict ordered En to join him in an archery display. The envoy asked, "I have heard that in Jingyuan there is a cavalry general named Wang—is this he?"

sentences.zh: 應曰：「然。」

translations.literal: He replied: "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: En answered, "It is."

sentences.zh: 射三發皆中，使以下相視皆歎息。

translations.literal: He shot three times and all hit; the envoy and those below exchanged glances and all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: He loosed three arrows and hit every time. The envoy and his party looked at one another and sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 出為涇原副都總管，並護秦、渭、延、熙四路兵，城西安，築臨羌、天都十餘壘。

translations.literal: He went out as deputy overall commander of Jingyuan, concurrently protecting the armies of Qin, Wei, Yan, and Xi routes, building Xi'an and constructing more than ten forts at Ling and Tian Du.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as deputy overall commander of Jingyuan, overseeing the armies of the Qin, Wei, Yan, and Xi circuits, building Xi'an and more than ten forts at Lingyang and Tiandu.

sentences.zh: 羌圍平夏，諸校欲出戰，恩曰：「賊傾國遠寇，難以爭鋒，宜以全制其敝。

translations.literal: The Qiang besieged Pingxia; the officers wished to sally out. En said: "The enemy has mobilized the whole state for a distant raid—hard to contest their edge; better to use wholeness to overcome their exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qiang besieged Pingxia, the officers wanted to sally out. En said, "The enemy has thrown the whole realm into this distant raid. We cannot match their momentum. Better to stay intact and wear them down.

sentences.zh: 彼野無所掠，必攜，攜而遇伏，必敗。」

translations.literal: In the wild they have nothing to plunder—they must grow weary; weary and then meeting ambush—they must be defeated."
translations.idiomatic: They have nothing to loot in the open country and will soon tire. Tired men who run into an ambush are sure to lose."

sentences.zh: 乃先行萬人設伏，羌既退師，果大獲。

translations.literal: He first led ten thousand men to set an ambush; when the Qiang withdrew their army, they indeed gained greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He sent ten thousand men ahead to lay an ambush. When the Qiang pulled back, the trap closed and the harvest was great.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，以衛州防禦使徙熙河，改知渭州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong took the throne, he was moved from Defense Commissioner of Weizhou to Xihe and changed to governing Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong came to the throne, En was transferred from defense commissioner of Weizhou to Xihe and appointed prefect of Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 括隱地二萬三千頃，分弓箭士耕屯，為三十一部，以省饋餉。

translations.literal: He registered hidden land of twenty-three thousand qing, divided bowmen-soldiers to farm garrison fields in thirty-one sections, to economize provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He registered twenty-three thousand qing of concealed land, assigned bowmen to farm it in thirty-one units, and so cut the cost of supplies.

sentences.zh: 邊臣獻車戰議，帝以訪恩，恩曰：「古有之，偏箱、鹿角，今相去益遠，人非所習，恐緩急難用。

translations.literal: A frontier minister presented a proposal for chariot warfare. The Emperor consulted En. En said: "The ancients had this—partial box formations, deer-horn arrays—but today distances grow ever greater; men are unaccustomed to them—I fear in urgent need they would be hard to use.
translations.idiomatic: A frontier official submitted a plan for chariot warfare. The Emperor asked En's view. En said, "The ancients used such things—the partial-box formation, the deer-horn array—but today the distances are greater still and the men are not trained in them. I fear that in a crisis they would prove useless.

sentences.zh: 夫操不習之器，與敵周旋，先自敗耳。」

translations.literal: To wield weapons one has not trained with and contend with the enemy is to defeat oneself first."
translations.idiomatic: To take up weapons you have never drilled with and go toe to toe with the enemy is to beat yourself before the fight even begins."

sentences.zh: 帝善其對。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was pleased with his answer.

sentences.zh: 遷馬步軍都指揮使、殿前都指揮使、武信軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Overall Commander of Horse and Foot Armies, Overall Commander of the Palace Front, and Military Commissioner of Wuxin.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to overall commander of the horse and foot armies, overall commander of the palace front guard, and military commissioner of Wuxin.

sentences.zh: 嘗汰禁卒數十人，樞密請命都承旨覆視，恩言：「朝廷選三帥，付以軍政，今去數十冗卒而不足信，即其他無可為者。」

translations.literal: Once he culled several tens of palace guard soldiers. The Bureau of Military Affairs requested the Chief Palace Aide-de-Camp to re-inspect. En said: "The court selects three commanders and entrusts them with military administration—if today removing several tens of redundant soldiers is not enough to trust us, then there is nothing else we can do."
translations.idiomatic: Once he dismissed several dozen palace guards. The Bureau of Military Affairs asked the chief palace aide-de-camp to review the decision. En said, "The court picks three commanders and gives them full military authority. If removing a few dozen excess troops is reason enough to doubt us, then there is nothing left for us to do at all."

sentences.zh: 帝立為罷之。

translations.literal: The Emperor immediately stopped it on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor at once called the review off.

sentences.zh: 眷顧甚寵，賜居宅，又賜城西地為園囿。

translations.literal: Favored with exceptional grace, he was granted a residence; also granted land west of the city as a garden park.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor favored him lavishly, giving him a residence and land west of the city for a private garden.

sentences.zh: 屬疾，以檢校司徒致仕。

translations.literal: When illness struck, he retired with the honorary title of Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, he retired with the honorary rank of grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 薨，年六十二，贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-two; posthumously conferred the Honorific of Grand General with Ceremonial Equivalence to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-two and was posthumously given the honorary title of grand general with ceremonial equivalence to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 楊應詢

translations.literal: Yang Yingxun
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yingxun

sentences.zh: 楊應詢。

translations.literal: Yang Yingxun.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yingxun.

sentences.zh: 字仲謀，章惠皇后族孫也。

translations.literal: Style name Zhongmou; a collateral descendant of Empress Zhanghui.
translations.idiomatic: His courtesy name was Zhongmou, and he was a kin of Empress Zhanghui.

sentences.zh: 曆知信安保定軍、霸州。

translations.literal: He successively governed Xin'an, Baoding Army, and Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as prefect of Xin'an, Baoding Army, and Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 塘濼之間地沮洳，水潦易集，居人浮板以濟。

translations.literal: Between the ponds and marshes the land was waterlogged; floods easily collected; residents used floating planks to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Between the ponds and marshes the land lay sodden and floods gathered easily; locals crossed on floating planks.

sentences.zh: 應詢增堤防為長衢，浚其旁以泄流，民利賴之。

translations.literal: Yingxun raised dikes into a long thoroughfare and dredged beside them to release the flow—the people benefited and relied on it.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxun built up the dikes into a raised road and dredged channels alongside to drain the water, to the lasting benefit of the people.

sentences.zh: 為河北沿邊安撫使。

translations.literal: He became Hebei Frontier Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed frontier pacification commissioner for Hebei.

sentences.zh: 徽宗以歸信、容城兩縣弓手為契丹所憚，欲增為千人，或恐生事，應詢曰：「吾欲備他盜，彼安能禁我？」

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong, because the bowmen of Guixin and Rongcheng counties were feared by the Khitan, wished to increase them to a thousand; some feared this would stir trouble. Yingxun said: "I wish to guard against other bandits—how can they forbid us?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong wanted to expand the bowmen of Guixin and Rongcheng counties to a thousand, since the Khitan feared them. Some worried this would provoke trouble. Yingxun said, "We mean to guard against other robbers—how can they stop us?"

sentences.zh: 卒增之。

translations.literal: In the end they were increased.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the force was expanded as planned.

sentences.zh: 知雄州，朝廷多取西夏地，契丹以姻婭為言，遣使乞還之，不得，擁兵並塞，中外恫疑。

translations.literal: As prefect of Xiongzhou—the court had taken much Western Xia territory; the Khitan spoke of marriage ties, sent envoys begging its return, and when refused massed troops along the border; court and country were alarmed and uncertain.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Xiong Prefecture, he faced a crisis: the court had seized large tracts from Western Xia, the Khitan cited marriage ties and sent envoys demanding restitution, and when refused they massed troops along the frontier. Alarm spread inside and outside the court.

sentences.zh: 應詢曰：「是特為虛聲嚇我耳。

translations.literal: Yingxun said: "This is merely empty noise to frighten us.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxun said, "This is only bluster meant to scare us.

sentences.zh: 願治兵積粟示有備，彼將聞風自戢。」

translations.literal: I wish to train troops and store grain to show preparedness—they will hear the wind and restrain themselves of their own accord."
translations.idiomatic: Let us drill the troops and stock grain to show we are ready—they will hear of it and pull back on their own."

sentences.zh: 明年，果還兵。

translations.literal: The next year, they indeed withdrew their troops.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Khitan army did withdraw.

sentences.zh: 復遣其相臣蕭保先、牛溫舒來請，詔應詢逆於境。

translations.literal: They again sent their chief ministers Xiao Baoxian and Niu Wenshu to petition; an edict ordered Yingxun to meet them at the border.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan sent their chief ministers Xiao Baoxian and Niu Wenshu again to press their case, and an edict ordered Yingxun to welcome them at the border.

sentences.zh: 既至，帝遣問所以來，應詢對：「願固守前議。」

translations.literal: When they arrived, the Emperor sent to ask why they had come. Yingxun replied: "I wish steadfastly to hold to the previous decision."
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, the Emperor asked what had brought them. Yingxun answered, "I ask only that we hold firm to our earlier decision."

sentences.zh: 尋兼高陽關路鈐轄。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Controller of the Gaoyang Pass Route.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also made controller of the Gaoyang Pass route.

sentences.zh: 邊人捕得北盜呂懺兒，契丹謂略執平民，有詔使縱釋。

translations.literal: Frontier men captured the northern bandit Lü Chan'er; the Khitan claimed he had been seized as a commoner by force; there was an edict to release him.
translations.idiomatic: Border troops captured the northern robber Lü Chan'er. The Khitan claimed he was an ordinary civilian seized by force, and an edict ordered his release.

sentences.zh: 應詢言：「吾知執盜耳，因其求而遂與之，是示以怯也。」

translations.literal: Yingxun said: "I know only that a bandit was seized—to yield him because they ask is to show weakness."
translations.idiomatic: Yingxun said, "I know only that we caught a thief. To hand him over the moment they demand it would show cowardice."

sentences.zh: 不與。

translations.literal: He did not yield him.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 遂質我民，固索之。

translations.literal: They then took our people as hostages and firmly demanded him back.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan then seized Song subjects as hostages and pressed the demand.

sentences.zh: 應詢以違詔貶秩，再遷洋州觀察使。

translations.literal: Yingxun was demoted in rank for violating the edict, then transferred again as Observation Commissioner of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxun was demoted for defying the edict and was later reassigned as observation commissioner of Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 入提舉萬壽觀。

translations.literal: He entered to supervise Wanshou Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed superintendent of Wanshou Abbey.

sentences.zh: 館契丹使，當賜柑而貢未至，有司代以他物，使不受，慶詢以言折之，乃下拜。

translations.literal: Hosting Khitan envoys, tangerines were due as gifts but the tribute shipment had not arrived; the relevant office substituted other items and the envoys refused them. Qing Xun refuted them in speech, and they then bowed in acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: While hosting Khitan envoys, tangerines were to be presented as gifts, but the tribute consignment had not yet arrived. The office offered substitutes, which the envoys refused until Yingxun talked them down; only then did they bow and accept.

sentences.zh: 復為定州、真定、大名副都總管。

translations.literal: He again served as deputy overall commander of Ding, Zhending, and Daming.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made deputy overall commander for Dingzhou, Zhending, and Daming.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十三，贈昭化軍節度使，諡曰康理。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-three; posthumously conferred Military Commissioner of Zhaohua; posthumous title Kangli.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-three, was posthumously made military commissioner of Zhaohua, and was given the posthumous name Kangli.

sentences.zh: 趙隆，字子漸，秦州成紀人。

translations.literal: Zhao Long, style name Zijian, was a native of Chengji in Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Long, courtesy name Zijian, was a native of Chengji in Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以勇敢應募，從王韶取熙河。

translations.literal: With courage he answered recruitment and followed Wang Shao to take Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: Volunteering for his bravery, he followed Wang Shao in the seizure of the Xihe region.

sentences.zh: 大將姚麟出戰，被重創，謂曰：「吾渴欲死，得水尚可活。」

translations.literal: The great general Yao Lin went out to battle, suffered grave wounds, and said to him: "I thirst and near death—get water and I can still live."
translations.idiomatic: General Yao Lin went into battle and was badly wounded. He said to Long, "I am parched to the point of death. Bring me water and I may yet survive."

sentences.zh: 時已暮，有泉近賊營，隆獨身潛往，漬衣泉中。

translations.literal: It was already dusk; there was a spring near the enemy camp; Long alone stole there secretly and soaked his clothes in the spring.
translations.idiomatic: It was already evening. A spring lay near the enemy camp. Long went alone and stole through to soak his garment in it.

sentences.zh: 賊覺，隆且鬥且行，得歸，持衣裂水以飲麟，麟乃蘇。

translations.literal: The enemy detected him; Long fought as he went and got back; holding the garment he wrung water for Lin to drink, and Lin then revived.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy spotted him, but Long fought his way back step by step. He wrung water from the soaked garment for Lin to drink, and Lin came round.

sentences.zh: 又從李憲破西市。

translations.literal: He again followed Li Xian to defeat Xishi.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Li Xian in the capture of Xishi.

sentences.zh: 師討鬼章，外河諸羌皆以兵應之。

translations.literal: When the army campaigned against Gui Zhang, all the Qiang beyond the river answered with troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched against Gui Zhang, Qiang tribes beyond the river all rallied to his aid with troops.

sentences.zh: 隆率眾先至，斧其橋，鬼章失援，乃成擒。

translations.literal: Long led the force to arrive first, cut down their bridge with axes; Gui Zhang lost support and was then captured.
translations.idiomatic: Long got there first with his men and chopped down the bridge with axes. Cut off from aid, Gui Zhang was taken alive.

sentences.zh: 為涇原將，戰平夏川，功最多。

translations.literal: As a Jingyuan general, in the battle of Pingxia Valley his merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: As a general on the Jingyuan front, he won the greatest credit in the battle of Pingxia Valley.

sentences.zh: 崇寧中，鈐轄熙河兵，將前軍出邈川，預復鄯、廓。

translations.literal: In the Chongning era, controlling Xihe troops, he led the vanguard out from Miaochuan, recovering Shan and Kuo in advance.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongning reign he commanded Xihe troops, led the vanguard out of Miaochuan, and helped recover Shan and Kuo.

sentences.zh: 夏人寇涇原，詔熙河深入分其兵，無令專鄉東方。

translations.literal: When Tanguts raided Jingyuan, an edict ordered Xihe to strike deep and divide their forces—not allowing them to concentrate solely toward the east.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut raided Jingyuan, an edict ordered the Xihe army to thrust deep and split the enemy force so they could not focus entirely on the east.

sentences.zh: 師至鐵山，隆先登，士皆殊死戰，夏人解去。

translations.literal: When the army reached Tieshan, Long climbed first; the soldiers all fought to the death; the Tangut withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At Iron Mountain Long was first over the top, and his men fought as if their lives depended on it. The Tangut broke off and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 召詣闕，徽宗慰勞之曰：「鐵山之戰，卿力也。」

translations.literal: Summoned to court, Emperor Huizong comforted and rewarded him, saying: "The battle of Tieshan was your doing."
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, Emperor Huizong praised him, saying, "The victory at Iron Mountain was yours."

sentences.zh: 童貫與論燕雲事，隆極言不可。

translations.literal: Tong Guan discussed the Yan-Yun affair with him; Long spoke out strongly that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Guan raised the subject of Yan and Yun with him, and Long insisted forcefully that the scheme must not be pursued.

sentences.zh: 貫曰：「君能共此，當有殊拜。」

translations.literal: Guan said: "If you can join in this, there will be an extraordinary promotion."
translations.idiomatic: Guan said, "If you will stand with me in this, you can expect an exceptional reward."

sentences.zh: 隆曰：「隆武夫，豈敢幹賞以敗祖宗二百年之好？

translations.literal: Long said: "Long is a martial man—how dare I seek reward and ruin the two hundred years of goodwill of the ancestral house?
translations.idiomatic: Long said, "I am only a soldier. How dare I grasp at reward and wreck two centuries of peace with our neighbors?

sentences.zh: 異時起釁，萬死不足謝責。」

translations.literal: If trouble arises in another day, ten thousand deaths would not suffice to answer for it."
translations.idiomatic: If war follows, a thousand deaths would not be enough to answer for my guilt."

sentences.zh: 貫知不可奪，白以知西寧州，充隴右都護。

translations.literal: Guan knew he could not be moved and reported him to govern Xining Prefecture, filling the post of Overall Protector of Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: Guan saw he could not be swayed and had him appointed prefect of Xining and overall protector of Longyou.

sentences.zh: 羌豪信服，十二種戶三萬六千，願屯內地。

translations.literal: Qiang chieftains trusted and submitted; twelve clans, thirty-six thousand households, wished to settle within the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang chieftains came to trust him, and thirty-six thousand households of twelve tribes asked to settle inland.

sentences.zh: 帥劉法西討，隆以奇兵襲羌，羌潰，城震武。

translations.literal: Marshal Liu Fa campaigned west; Long with surprise troops raided the Qiang; the Qiang broke; they walled Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Marshal Liu Fa marched west, Long struck the Qiang with a flanking force. The Qiang broke, and the fort at Zhenwu was built.

sentences.zh: 遷溫州防禦使，龍神衛、捧日天武都指揮使，仍為本道馬步副都總管。

translations.literal: Promoted to Defense Commissioner of Wenzhou, Overall Commander of Dragon Spirit Guard and Sun-and-Moon Celestial Martial Guard, still serving as deputy overall commander of horse and foot in that circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to defense commissioner of Wenzhou, overall commander of the Dragon Spirit and Sun-and-Moon Celestial Martial guards, while remaining deputy overall commander of horse and foot for the circuit.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈鎮潼軍節度使，命詞臣制碑，帝篆額曰「旌忠」。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously conferred Military Commissioner of Zhentong Army; ordered court literary men to compose a stele; the Emperor inscribed the header "Commemorating Loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made military commissioner of Zhentong, a court scholar was ordered to compose a stele inscription, and the Emperor personally wrote the heading "Commemorating Loyalty."

sentences.zh: 論曰：有國家者不可忘武備，故高祖以馬上得天下，而猶有「安得猛士守四方」之歎。

translations.literal: Commentary says: one who has a state must not forget martial preparedness—thus even Gaozu, who won the realm on horseback, still had the sigh "Where can I find fierce warriors to guard the four quarters?"
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: rulers of a state must never neglect military readiness. Even Gaozu, who won the empire from horseback, still lamented, "Where shall I find bold men to guard the four corners of the realm?"

sentences.zh: 然所貴為將領者，非取其武勇而已也，必忠以為主，智以為本，勇以為用，及其成功，雖有小大之殊，俱足以尊主庇民也。

translations.literal: Yet what is prized in generals is not martial valor alone—loyalty must be the foundation, wisdom the root, courage the instrument; when they succeed, though there are differences great and small, all alike suffice to honor the ruler and shelter the people.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what we esteem in a commander is not brawn alone. Loyalty must be the foundation, wisdom the root, courage the tool. When such men succeed, their deeds may differ in scale, but each alike honors the throne and shields the people.

sentences.zh: 苗授策篯南之不可城，履不肯討阿章，永清不以地與敵，文鬱撫納香崖，紹能之忠勇，珍之忠樸好義，光祖、應詢明於料敵，守約及整禦眾嚴明，斌、浩之善戰，岩、恩之善射，闃之出則先登，入則殿后，其材雖殊，其可以任奔走禦侮之責於四境則一也。

translations.literal: Miao Shou counseled that fortifying Zhainan was impossible; Lü refused to campaign against A Zhang; Yongqing would not yield land to the enemy; Wenyu pacified and received Xiangya; Shaoneng's loyal courage; Zhen's loyal plainness and love of righteousness; Guangzu and Yingxun were clear in estimating the enemy; Shouyue and Zheng were strict and clear in commanding troops; Bin and Hao were skilled in battle; Yan and En were skilled in archery; Qu, going out was first to climb, entering was rearguard—their talents differed, yet their capacity to bear the charge of rushing about and repelling insult on the four borders was one.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Shou judged that Zhainan could not be walled; Lü would not march against A Zhang; Yongqing refused to surrender territory to the enemy; Wenyu pacified and won over Xiangya; Shaoneng showed loyal courage; Zhen was loyal, plain, and devoted to duty; Guangzu and Yingxun read the enemy with clear judgment; Shouyue and Zheng were stern and precise in command; Bin and Hao excelled in battle; Yan and En excelled in archery; Qu was first over the wall going out and last in line coming back. Their gifts differed, but each could equally bear the work of racing the borders to beat back threats.

sentences.zh: 成以捍衛邊陲，服勤致死，明詔褒飭，廟食一方，宜哉。

translations.literal: Cheng, in defending the frontier borders, served with diligence unto death—bright edicts praised and admonished; temple sacrifice in one region—fitting indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Cheng defended the frontier and served until death; imperial edicts praised him, and local temples enshrined him—a fitting honor.

sentences.zh: 君萬挾誣報怨，贍狡譎喜功，國有常罰，父子謫死，亦宜也。

translations.literal: Junwan used false charges to repay a grudge; Zhan was crafty, cunning, and fond of glory—the state has fixed punishments; father and son condemned to death—also fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Junwan used false accusations to settle scores; Zhan was sly, devious, and hungry for glory. The state has its fixed penalties—father and son condemned to die—and that was only just.

sentences.zh: 詵首取燕，終變其說，既黜旋復，為失刑矣。

translations.literal: Shen first urged taking Yan, then finally changed his position; once dismissed yet soon restored—in this the law was misapplied.
translations.idiomatic: Shen first championed the seizure of Yan, then reversed himself. Dismissed one day and restored the next—that was a failure of justice.

sentences.zh: 至若仲武敗則引咎責己，勝則不自言功，隆不敢啟釁幹賞，蘊甘分而辭榮，有士君子之行焉，尤武士之所難能也。

translations.literal: As for Zhongwu, defeat then he took blame upon himself; victory then he did not claim merit himself; Long did not dare provoke trouble to grasp reward; Yun willingly accepted his lot and declined glory—they had the conduct of scholar-gentlemen, especially what martial knights find hardest to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu, when defeated, blamed himself; when victorious, he claimed no credit. Long would not stir up war for reward. Yun was content with his station and turned away honors. Such men showed the conduct of true gentlemen—something especially rare among soldiers.
